articles.title: El Elche aplica la máxima pena al Rayo
articles.standfirst: Los de Anselmi golean en Vallecas con dos tantos de penalti y dejan muy tocado al equipo madrileño, que falló un lanzamiento desde los once metros con 0-2
articles.summary: Los de Anselmi golean en Vallecas con dos tantos de penalti y dejan muy tocado al equipo madrileño, que falló un lanzamiento desde los once metros con 0-2
articles.body: El Elche sumó su segundo triunfo de la temporada, segundo a domicilio, en Vallecas gracias a una gran actuación ante un Rayo que fue deshaciéndose con el paso de los minutos. En un estadio algo más apagado de lo normal, los de Anselmi golearon gracias a dos goles de penalti de Redondo y de Niño y a un tercero de Valera en el segundo tiempo. Antes, con 0-2, Ciss mandó una pena máxima al larguero que podría haber cambiado todo. Con un ambiente enrarecido tras lo ocurrido ante el Athletic y con la expectación sobre si habría nuevas protestas en el estadio, el Rayo arrancó bien. Lanzado. De hecho, a los 40 segundos ya reclamaron un penalti por un manotazo de Sangaré sobre Álvaro que el árbitro no consideró punible. Eso sí, el efecto inicial apenas duró 15 minutos, con Camello teniendo las dos mejores para los locales. La segunda, con todo a favor en la semiluna tras un pase atrás de Pedrosa que mandó arriba con todo a favor. Sin embargo, con el paso de los minutos, el equipo empezó a partirse, el Elche a hilar buenas jugadas y ser profundo… y ahí empezó a llegar el jaleo. Cepeda y Villar avisaron probando a Audero, que vio poco después como Lejeune derribaba a Revivo dentro del área y el colegiado señalaba penalti. Ahí llegó Redondo para abrir la lata con un disparo a media altura que adivinó el guardameta, aunque su estirada no fue suficiente para evitar el 0-1. Se rozaba la media hora y los de Anselmi se soltaron la melena, de nuevo con Revivo haciendo protagonista a Audero y con Fer Niño probando la madera de su portería con un buen remate en el área. Y, precisamente este último, sería el que aumentaría la renta de los suyos tras un penalti de Ciss, precipitado, derribando a Lemar que tuvo que comprobarse en el monitor de VAR. Ahí el ariete, que ya lleva seis dianas, no falló y engañó al meta rayista. Dos penaltis, dos goles... pero habría más, esta vez para el otro bando. Una mano de Sangaré, que pasaba por ahí cuando Álvaro bajaba en el área rival un balón llovido, fue señalado como infracción y Ciss, con la idea de lamer sus heridas tras el cometido en su propio área, se atrevió con el lanzamiento. A pesar de ello, la valentía no fue premiada y el larguero escupió su derechazo. El Elche siguió creciendo y los de la franja, cuando podían maquillar un poco el panorama y afrontar de otra manera la segunda parte, se dieron de bruces contra un muro. De hecho, pudo ser peor si Audero, el mejor de los de Beñat San José, no hubiese sacado una mano brutal a un cabezazo a bocajarro de Revivo en el añadido del primer acto. Tras el paso por vestuarios, los rayistas salieron de nuevo con todo, con Tsitaishvili como hombre de refresco y referencia para agitar el avispero. Sólo su mera actitud de coger la pelota, encargar hacia adentro y buscar un tiro o un centro ya encendía al Estadio de Vallecas. Pero, como decía antes, no era el día del Rayo. La más clara al inicio la tuvo Pedro Díaz, que tras un par de indecisiones en defensa del Elche, sacó un derechazo directo a la escuadra que tapó con mano firme un segurísimo Dituro. Y, como era de prever, los visitantes, bien armados, tranquilos y seguros, esperaban con el paso de los minutos ir encontrando espacios al contragolpe para sellar el triunfo. Así se fue rompiendo el partido, convirtiéndose en un ida y vuelta gracias también a las imprecisiones de ambos bandos. Y en una de esas jugadas, Valera aprovechó un buen balón de Buonanotte en el ecuador del segundo acto para definir con clase, picadita, ante Audero. Aquello dejó K.O. a los madrileños, que incluso tuvieron que dar 'gracias' por no recibir más tantos. Tete Morente, que salió en el tramo final para seguir aportando picante, vio cómo la cruceta le devolvía una volea 'a lo Mendieta' que hubiese sido otro puñal en el corazón vallecano. Al final, tres puntos que viajan hacia Elche y que permiten respirar a los ilicitanos fuera del descenso... y oportunidad perdida en Vallecas para recuperar una alegría que, con todo lo ocurrido fuera del terreno de juego, era más que necesaria.

articles.title: Tablas en Butarque en el estreno de Carrión para cortar la sangría
articles.standfirst: Álex Millán neutralizó el gol de Luvumbo y el Lega vuelve a puntuar cinco jornadas después, mientras el Mallorca no logra su segundo triunfo foráneo
articles.summary: Álex Millán neutralizó el gol de Luvumbo y el Lega vuelve a puntuar cinco jornadas después, mientras el Mallorca no logra su segundo triunfo foráneo
articles.body: Leganés y Mallorca firmaron tablas en el Ontime Butarque en el estreno de Luis Carrión en el banquillo pepinero, que al menos corta la racha negativa de cuatro derrotas seguidas sin goles a favor que provocó la destitución de Rubén Albés aunque sigue sin reencontrarse con la victoria. Por su parte, el cuadro bermellón supo competir y encadena su quinto desplazamiento sumando, pero sigue sin lograr su segundo triunfo a domicilio. Tras una primera parte de mayor dominio bermellón, al descanso se llegó con ventaja visitante tras el gol de Zito Luvumbo superada la media hora al aprovechar el rechace de Raúl Fernández a disparo de Pablo Torre. Un tanto que volvió a poner cuesta arriba el encuentro para un Leganés necesitado de resultados y confianza. El propio angoleño había sido el primero en probar fortuna con una semi chilena que salió rozando el poste, mientras Rubén Peña, con una gran acción individual pero cuyo remate fue taponado por la defensa bermellona, y Álex Sancris, con un disparo con mucho efecto al que respondió con gran acierto Arnau Tenas, tuvieron las ocasiones más claras para el equipo pepinero. El Lega salió decidido a encontrar el empate en la reanudación y de hecho la tuvieron Gharbi y Soko, pero sus remates cercanos volvieron a golpear en Valjent y Raíllo, respectivamente. Finalmente fue Álex Millán el que logró la igualada al rematar en el área pequeña el centro de Álex Sancris devolviendo la ilusión a Butarque. El delantero puso fin, además, a una preocupante sequía goleadora de cuatro encuentros consecutivos sin marcar. Carrión buscó soluciones desde el banquillo, dando entrada a Zico, Naim, Unax del Cura, Kechta y Andrés Campos. El Mallorca también movió sus piezas para mantener el equilibrio y defender un resultado que le permitía puntuar a domicilio. Incluso pudo llevarse la victoria, con una clara ocasión para Calatayud, cuyo remate picado salió rozando el poste. Sin embargo, Arnau Tenas evitó en el añadido el segundo del Lega a cabezazo de Unax del Cura. Un reparto de puntos que deja sensaciones diferentes. El Lega detiene la sangría de derrotas y comienza una nueva etapa con Carrión, pero aún tiene trabajo por delante para recuperar su mejor versión. Y el Mallorca se lleva un punto de Butarque para seguir en la parte alta de la tabla.

articles.title: El Racing remonta y el Espanyol no
articles.standfirst: Zabiri sella la victoria de los de Santander en un duelo que empezaron perdiendo
articles.summary: Zabiri sella la victoria de los de Santander en un duelo que empezaron perdiendo
articles.body: A lo bueno se acostumbra uno rápido. En Santander ya caminan por la calle como si llevasen veinte años seguidos en Primera. Nadie se acuerda de las penurias en momentos de alegría. El equipo de José Alberto juega bien, divierte y, lo más importante, gana. Incluso los partidos que se le tuercen cuando está siendo mejor que el rival, con lo que frustra eso a un recién ascendido. Al Espanyol le hicieron sentir un equipo menor. Lo que tal vez sean ahora mismo. El Racing salió a unir los puntos, a coser las jugadas con cuantas más puntadas mejor. Hay equipos que deciden buscar la salvación comprando latas y comida deshidratada para situaciones de emergencia, pero en Santander han llenado la nevera de productos frescos y tienen una despensa de jugones que ya quisieran algunos equipos a los que se espera en la zona alta. Los de José Alberto tenían más balón, llegaron más y sólo el partidazo del portero rival evitó que se fueran al descanso con ventaja. Fortuño evitó el gol de Canales a la media hora con un paradón y en el córner Zabiri no atinó con la portería. El Espanyol dibujaba líneas rectas, vectores que viajaban desde la defensa hacia el ataque sin pasar por el centro del campo, pero casi encuentra premio. Pablo Ramón cortó con la mano un balón en el área y Gil Manzano, que no lo pitó en directo, fue al monitor. Lo que acabó señalando fue una falta anterior de Roberto Fernández sobre Belocian que tampoco había visto en juego. Del intermedio volvió mejor el Racing, pero Fortuño siguió negando el gol a los locales y, tras un doble paradón a la hora de juego, sus compañeros le agradecieron los servicios prestados. Javi Hernández dio su sexta asistencia (las mismas que Lamine, los que más de LaLiga) para que Edu Expósito, desde dentro del área, superase a Agirrezabala. El Racing se revolvió y se negó a perder un partido en el que estaba siendo mejor. Pablo García azuzó el avispero, Belocian cazó un rechace y probó un disparo lejano que se le coló a Fortuño junto al palo y en Santander tocaron a rebato. Los de José Alberto atacaron el área por saturación y, en un barullo tras un córner, Zabiri acabó empujando la bola al fondo de la red, para desesperación de Manolo González. El Espanyol cae al descenso y, pese a los buenos nombres que salpican su plantilla, tiene mala cara. Algo pasa en un equipo que parece resignado en octubre.

articles.title: De Jong: "Nunca he estado en el banquillo mucho tiempo, y espero no tener que hacerlo este curso"
articles.standfirst: El medio está ya preparado para sumar minutos tras su grave lesión de rodilla
articles.summary: El medio está ya preparado para sumar minutos tras su grave lesión de rodilla
articles.body: Frenkie de Jong entró en las últimas convocatorias del Barça, en LaLiga contra el Betis y en la Champions contra el PSG, pero aún no ha tenido minutos tras la rotura de ligamento de la rodilla que sufrió durante el Mundial. El centrocampista neerlandés, de 29 años, habló, en las últimas horas, con Ziggo Sport, donde repasó su difícil situación, la competencia con Rodri, sus ambiciones, las críticas que recibe... Competencia y Rodri "Estoy contento con la llegada de Rodri, porque es un jugador de calidad. Ya tenemos varios mediocampistas excelentes, por lo que la competencia es intensa, pero lo veo como un gran desafío para mí". Rol reducido "Nunca he experimentado estar en el banquillo durante un período prolongado, y espero no tener que hacerlo esta temporada. Ahora estoy completamente en forma, me pongo más fuerte cada día, y espero jugar más minutos pronto. Sé que necesito volver de forma gradual, pero mi objetivo a largo plazo es jugar regularmente y regresar al once inicial lo antes posible”. Regreso "Me encuentro muy bien y me siento preparado". Cambio de ubicación "Si el entrenador o el equipo me lo piden, siempre lo haré. Pero creo que todo el mundo sabe que soy centrocampista". Ambición "Ganar la Champions es algo que todavía tengo pendiente en mi carrera. Es un gran objetivo, un sueño, un deseo". Críticas "Siempre ha sido así: la mayoría de las críticas hacia mí, o el ruido que se genera, llegan cuando no estoy, cuando no puedo jugar al fútbol. Esta vez volvió a pasar y entiendo perfectamente de dónde viene...". Frustración grada culé "Entiendo muy bien a los aficionados. Me ven jugar con la selección y no con el equipo al que apoyan. Si lo simplificas, es así: jugué el Mundial hasta el último partido y después estuve tres meses de baja. Entiendo perfectamente ese sentimiento". Frustración personal "Yo soy el primero al que le resulta desagradable, junto con el club y los aficionados, porque quiero jugar. No pude hacerlo, la lesión resultó ser más grave de lo que pensábamos. Entonces, empiezan a circular todo tipo de historias y pasan muchas cosas...".

articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: La Liga – El Clasico preview, predictions, teams
articles.summary: Bragging rights are up for grabs in Sunday’s El Clasico between La Liga leaders Barcelona and third-placed Real Madrid.
articles.body:
Who : Barcelona vs Real Madrid What : La Liga, El Clasico Where : Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain When : Sunday at 9pm (20:00 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 17:00 GMT.

For weeks La Liga leaders Barcelona have been eagerly awaiting Sunday’s El Clasico as a chance to stretch the gap between themselves and rivals Real Madrid to a massive nine points.

Some turbulence in the final approach to the clash at Camp Nou has complicated the picture for Hansi Flick’s Spanish champions, who suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday.

By contrast, Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches, thrashing RB Leipzig on Wednesday and starting to look, for the first time since Jose Mourinho’s arrival this summer, like a team.

Should Real come away with a win, it would not only halve the current six-point gap, but ⁠provide a much-needed confidence boost for a side that has lost six of the last seven Clasicos.

Mourinho’s return to the fixture will attract the most attention of all.

The ⁠63-year-old is a veteran of 27 matches against Barcelona and 17 El Clasicos on ⁠the Real bench.

Real Madrid President Florentino Perez first appointed Mourinho as manager in 2010 to compete with Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona, and he will hope the Portuguese can wrest the La Liga title back to the Bernabeu for a second time.

Mourinho’s first spell at Real coincided with arguably the most heated encounters in ‌the modern history of El Clasico, and there will be numerous cameras trained on his every move at Camp Nou on Sunday.

The Portuguese manager won just once in his first 10 El Clasicos but went unbeaten in his final five games ‌against ‌Barcelona, recording three victories.

Unfair to compare us with Barca, Mourinho says

Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy.

Mourinho highlighted that he has been at the helm only a few months in comparison with Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024.

“People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished, … but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” Mourinho continued.

“We’ve been working for three months. Out of that you can take preseason when the players were arriving [back from the World Cup] and the recent international break. Then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months.

“This is the start of a product. We’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths. The players are learning about the coach. … Comparing a team in this state [to more established sides], I think is unfair.”

The German coach said he expected a Madrid side arriving with “a lot of confidence” and praised Mourinho.

“I have the highest respect. When you’re managing teams on this level for so many years and you always have success, it’s about quality. He showed this at every club,” Flick told reporters.

“Every player from the [German] national team who worked under him speaks with a great respect. I think the same. He’s a colleague, a very, very successful colleague and a great colleague.”

Flick said the 4-2 defeat in Paris by PSG on Tuesday gave his team some clues as to where they need to improve.

“We analysed this game. We did many things really good, but we saw some situations where we have to improve,” Flick said.

“We have to grow as a team. Tomorrow we play against one of the best teams in the world, so it’s a good opportunity to grow, to challenge ourselves, to improve ourselves and to grow as a team.”

Managers on ‘incredible’, ‘unique’ El Clasico

Flick: “El Clasico is different. It is the best match in our sport, and everyone will watch it. It is incredible. It is true that we are playing for just three points, but the importance of the match goes far beyond that.”

Mourinho: “We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in El Clasico, it doesn’t matter what you did before. It has no influence. El Clasico is unique. Normally, the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully, it’s a great game and we win.”

Barcelona have a perfect record in La Liga with nine wins from nine games. They are five points clear at the top of the standings.

Their only defeat in all competitions this season came in the last match, in which they fell 4-2 to title holders PSG in the Champions League league phase.

How have Real Madrid played this season?

Real are third in the La Liga points table, six points behind leaders and rivals Barca.

They have won seven league games but lost to Atletico Madrid and Real Betis .

However, Real have made a perfect start in the UCL, registering two wins in as many matches.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Barcelona a 54.4 percent chance of winning this Clasico while Real have a 26.1 percent probability. There are 19.5 percent odds of a draw.

Overall, Barca are given a 77.93 percent chance of retaining the title this season with Real tipped to finish second and Atletico third.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Martin Ho wants 'more support' for WSL referees
articles.summary: Tottenham manager Martin Ho was frustrated by a penalty decision in their defeat by Arsenal and says Women's Super League referees "need more support".
articles.body:
Tottenham manager Martin Ho says Women's Super League referees "need more support" as he vented his frustration over a controversial penalty decision in their derby defeat by Arsenal.

A 2-1 win for the Gunners at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday was settled by Alessia Russo's spot-kick in the 56th minute.

Referee Phoebe Cross awarded the decision after Lisa Baum's shot bounced off the post and Cathinka Tandberg's clearance hit Spurs team-mate Ella Morris' outstretched hand.

According to the laws, if the ball hits a hand after it was played by a team-mate, an indirect free-kick should be awarded.

Ho said: "My interpretation of the rule is if your team-mate hits it and your team-mate is one yard away, time and distance is taken into account and it's not a penalty.

"That's what we were told at the start of the season in the referee's meeting. I asked the question, 'how is it [a penalty] from that distance?' They couldn't give me an answer on the pitch.

"I said I would come and speak to them after the game because I want to understand it, I want to understand what they're seeing. Then I can accept a decision that is there. When that decides a game, it's frustrating, because it's not within the laws of the game."

Ho admitted WSL referees have "a hard enough job" to do, but believes the standards have "got worse than last year".

There is currently no use of video assistant referees (VAR) or goalline technology in the WSL, while not all officials are full-time.

Earlier this month, the Guardian reported , external the wait for full-time WSL referees was set to continue until 2029 despite a recent funding boost.

Asked how standards could improve, Ho added: "They need more support and more full-time [referees].

"I understand there is probably a rule where they can't do more than one game on a weekend and that's nothing against any of the referees, but they had an elite referee [Lisa Benn] on the side the pitch. For a big game, put them in the middle.

"I think that's where they need more support, more training, because when you look at most decisions that are going on, there's a lot of controversy in a lot of games.

"We got two bookings in the first half but we were being dragged back by the shirt by Arsenal players and didn't get anything. That's probably the frustrating part."

BBC Sport has contacted WSL Football for a response.

articles.title: Javier Solís, sobre el desembarco de Pitchwise en el Valencia: "Los recursos irán al césped..."
articles.standfirst: El director general del club analiza la venta del 42% de las acciones de la familia Lim y el futuro del club
articles.summary: El director general del club analiza la venta del 42% de las acciones de la familia Lim y el futuro del club
articles.body: Javier Solís, director general del Valencia, tomó la palabra antes del partido ante el Villarreal sobre el césped de Mestalla. Con la venta del 42% de las acciones de Peter Lim a Pitchwise, un fondo de inversión americano aún caliente, el director general del club analizó la venta: "Los recursos irán al césped y también a instalaciones, veremos dónde hacen falta mejoras". Javier Solís, director general del Valencia, analizó en Movistar el desembarco de Pitchtwise como accionista de la sociedad, con la compra del 42% de las acciones, y una inyección de capital de 100 millones de euros. "Es el inicio de una nueva etapa, muy importante para el club la llegada de Pitchwise, con dos grandes ejecutivos como Ann Rodriguez y Corey Woolfolk, que van a aportar toda su experiencia con su trabajo en el día a día del club" ¿Qué cambiará en el club? "Cambiarán cosas a mejor con la entrada de Anne y Corey; van a aportar su experiencia, habrá que integrar los flujos de trabajo para ver cómo nos intercomunicamos. Es un paso adelante y una nueva etapa para el club, sin duda"". Aportación al club 100 millones, ¿a dónde se destinarán? "Ahora es cuando empieza el trabajo de campo, ver dónde van los recursos: irán al césped pero también a instalaciones, ahora empieza el trabajo para analizar y ver dónde hacen falta mejoras". El Valencia será un gran aliciente en el mercado. "El mercado está ahí, trabajaremos para mejorar el equipo el mensaje es de optimismo, una nueva etapa que empieza y que es muy ilusionante para el club".

articles.title: St Mirren 2-0 Dundee: Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule fire Buddies to victory
articles.summary: Report as goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule give St Mirren a 2-0 victory over Dundee
articles.body:
Wing-back Ramsay fired Saints ahead in the 20th minute with his first goal since joining the club on loan in the summer.

Sule doubled the lead for the Buddies in the 57th minute to give his side a real grip of the game.

Dundee pulled a goal back in the 73rd minute through Bradley Fink after a decent spell of pressure but the visitors could not find an equaliser.

St Mirren were first to threaten as the wintry conditions played a role in the early stages. Ismeal Kabia unleashed a shot from the edge of the box, but it was held by Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

The home side made the breakthrough when Sule broke down the righ before playing the ball across goal into the path of Ramsay, whose shot trickled over the line with the block from Goodman unable to keep it out.

The Saints loanee almost doubled his tally when he rose to meet a free-kick from the left. His header fell straight into the arms of Goodman, who then spilled the ball before it was scrambled clear.

Sule turned scorer in the second-half to give St Mirren full command of the match. A cross from Killian Phillips was met by the head of the attacker on the edge of the six-yard box to double the home side's lead.

Dundee pushed to get a foothold back in the game with Ashley Hay bulleting a header narrowly wide from close range.

The visitors did eventually pull a goal back through Fink. St Mirren keeper Jacob Chapman saved the initial shot only for the Dundee striker to knock the ball home at the second attempt.

The away side pushed for an equaliser in the latter stages, but the Buddies held on to claim all three points, much to the delight of a delirious but sodden home crowd.

"I'm delighted for the group. They probably needed something like that.

"It's easy for me to keep saying the same messages and keep talking to them about their confidence and belief and what we're trying to do, but when you go on a run like we've been on, it can be difficult for the players at times.

"We had one really good run, we've had a poor run, hopefully that's us coming out of it now as well."

"In the first half we showed a lot of bravery in possession, in terms of our build-up and in controlling the game, but we didn't ask enough questions of them defensively.

"We spoke prior to the game about that particular fact: that we must ask questions of them defensively in a variety of ways. We didn't ask enough of them.

"Credit to St Mirren. They've gone through a difficult period, and they showed a lot of resilience today."

articles.title: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone: Kevin Kelsy scores two, with Ryan Naderi and Tochi Chukwuani also on target as Rangers cut Celtic’s lead at the top
articles.summary: Report as Kevin Kelsy scores twice with Ryan Naderi and Tochi Chukwuani also on the scoresheet; Rangers beat St Johnstone 4-0 to cut Celtic’s lead at top of Scottish Premiership
articles.body:
Kelsy opened the scoring in the first half when Ryan Naderi unselfishly squared to his strike partner to tap in after being played through by Minsu Kim.

St Johnstone made a triple substitution at the break and were on top when Naderi scored for Rangers against the run of play, bundling in after Toby Steward spilled a shot from Kim.

The home side extended their lead further when Kelsy was on hand at the back post to divert a header from Emmanuel Fernandez into the net.

Substitute Tochi Chukwuani added gloss to the win with the fourth when he turned in Djeidi Gassama's cross to move Rangers one point behind Celtic, who travel to Edinburgh to take on Hibernian live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

"It's quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and created so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time.

"And obviously, we don't want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

"I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good.

"I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be?

"And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.

"We have no divine right to expect a 90-odd minute dominant performance, St Johnstone are a good side in their own right and they're doing well so.

"But it's ironic we score three goals second half when we were weren't as polished and as clean with our work.

"To score three goals in a second half where we weren't as good, in the first half we were completely dominant and very good and we only get the one.

"So there's lots of learnings for us here, but I actually think that you get your strikers scoring goals, a clean sheet and another win just chalked off on what was was a horrible day for everybody, it was just important that we won the game."

"Rangers were very strong in the first half. They put us under a lot of pressure and got their goal.

"For 15 minutes in the second half we had momentum at 1-0 down.

"The logic of the situation is that if you don't take your chances the top teams will score, which they did.

"You can't ask for better chances than the ones we got in this match. You've got to hit the target and ask questions of the goalkeeper.

"That's the biggest disappointment we have from this match."

articles.title: Arsenal 2-0 Everton: Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel move the champions level on points with leaders Man City
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Arsenal produce the perfect response to Man City's first slip-up in the Premier League to go level on points thanks to goals from defenders Ezri Konsa - his first for the club - and Gabriel on his 200th league appearance for the Gunners
articles.body:
Ezri Konsa poked in at the back post after seven minutes to score a scrappy first goal for the club and end Arsenal's wait for a first non-penalty set-piece goal of the season before Gabriel's second-half header sealed the win on his 200th Premier League appearance.

Arsenal, buoyed by the news of City's first league defeat this season, were as relentless as the north London rain as they made it seven wins from eight in the league to keep up with their rivals on 21 points, behind only on goal difference.

Viktor Gyokeres, handed his first league start of the season, failed to get off the mark for the campaign but was credited with the assist for Konsa's opener, making it two from two after setting up Declan Rice's equaliser in Wednesday's 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich .

Everton, now winless in 14 league trips to Arsenal, were handed a big chance to equalise at 1-0 just before half-time but Thierno Barry failed to make the most of Ben White's weak headed back pass to goalkeeper David Raya.

David Moyes' depleted side, without Jack Grealish and Jarrad Branthwaite at Arsenal, were unbeaten in the league until last weekend, but have now suffered back-to-back defeats and remain without an away win in the competition after the fourth attempt.

Arteta reveals he clips up managers stepping out of tech area

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta received his second yellow card of the season for stepping out of his technical area which prompted a bizarre revelation from the Spaniard after full-time.

Arteta, now one booking away from a suspension, said he clips up other Premier League managers committing the same infraction and is prepared to present the proof in defence of himself.

"There are managers that have the record in the league," the Arsenal manager said after the game. "Thirty-six times in 10 minutes they leave the touchline. No yellows [for them]. So I'm clipping all of that.

"I have a massive storage of images. If somebody come to say [something to me. I can say] I'm not the record yet.

"Somebody else has the record. Then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don't know where we're going to be."

Arteta: I love the mentality of this team!

"We're very happy with the victory, with the performance and with the week, because we were given a terrible schedule.

"We have overcome every hurdle, on top of some injuries. I love the mentality of the team and the quality we've shown."

On Gabriel overcoming injury scare: "He's a clear example. When I'm talking about the mentality of the team, obviously the mentality of the team is the mentality of the individuals in the team.

"Gabi is a great example of that, because we were all scared. Not because of the way he went down, but the reaction of the players that we're next to him. Immediately he says that he wants to continue and then he scores a goal to help us to win the game. That's what we need from our players."

On Konsa's impressive adaptation to Arsenal: "Unbelievable. To come to a huge club like Arsenal, with no pre-season, when William Saliba and the other players that are already here.

"To position yourself in that manner, with that naturality, and performing at the level that he's doing and building already a chemistry and a partnership with Gabi that seems so solid is very difficult to do and we are lucky to have him."

"We didn't really get to a level which I think would have been good enough to win on the day. We gave away a goal very early which meant we were chasing.

"We got a bit better in the second half, got back into it a little bit more, got a bit closer to Arsenal and then they came up with the second goal. Some good stuff, certainly on the defensive side of it.

"I didn't feel we'd done enough on the attacking part of the game."

articles.title: Nicolas Jackson: Striker caps fine start to Aston Villa career with two goals to beat Manchester City
articles.summary: Nicolas Jackson continues an excellent start to his Aston Villa career with a match-winning double against Manchester City.
articles.body:
Nicolas Jackson's double to defeat Manchester City on Saturday capped an excellent start to the striker's spell at Aston Villa .

Signed from Chelsea as a direct replacement for Ollie Watkins - Villa's main source of goals for the previous six seasons - it was imperative the 25-year-old Senegal international hit the ground running in claret and blue.

Jackson has done just that, scoring seven goals in his first 11 appearances for Villa - six in the last six - and helping his new side to a 100% start in the Champions League and spearheading their recovery after a slow start to the Premier League campaign.

"The players, the manager, the team - everything is incredible," Jackson told BBC Match of the Day.

"I'm very happy that I'm here and hopefully we can do amazing things together."

Jackson spent two full seasons at Chelsea after joining in 2023 and had a year on loan at German giants Bayern Munich before moving to Villa in the summer for a deal worth up to £65m.

There is a much smaller sample size from his time at Villa Park compared with his spell at Stamford Bridge, but on several metrics, he is showing signs of improvement.

Jackson scored 24 goals in 65 Premier League appearances for Chelsea , netting every 210 minutes on average, with a shot conversion rate of 15%.

That compares with four in seven games for Villa, averaging a goal every 138 minutes with a shot conversion rate of 21%.

One of the criticisms of Jackson at Chelsea was he had lots of chances and did not convert as many of them as he should.

In his early weeks at Villa, he is outperforming his expected goals tally by exactly two.

Both of their shots on target against City came from Jackson's right foot - and both ended up in the net.

'He looks like a really good piece of business' - Keown

England international Watkins scored 91 Premier League goals in 221 league appearances for Villa before moving to Saudi Arabia club Al-Hilal in August.

He was a consistent scorer, never failing to reach double figures for Premier League goals during each of his six seasons with the club.

The respective statistics of Jackson and Watkins from last season suggest Jackson is more involved in general play than the England forward, while also being involved in more chances.

If Jackson's current run of form continues, his fee may prove to be a bargain.

Former Villa and England defender Martin Keown told BBC Sport: "I've liked him all season. I think he's key to Villa's success.

"I think he's an upgrade on Ollie Watkins, I really do.

"Ollie was magnificent for them, but this guy is more of a predator [in and around the penalty area]. Pace will always trouble top defenders and he's got it in abundance.

"I think having worked with the manager before at Villarreal, he's sort of fast-tracking his quick development.

"He looks like a really good piece of business right now."

Jackson double for Villa ends Man City's 100% start

Jackson stars with two goals - player ratings for Aston Villa v Man City

'So many players improve and thrive' under Emery

Saturday's win was achieved on the fourth anniversary of Emery's appointment as Villa boss.

Under the Spaniard, they have become fixtures in the upper echelons of the Premier League, regulars in European competition and ended a 30-year wait for a major trophy by winning the Europa League.

Results are one thing, but there are also numerous examples of players who have been rejuvenated or scaled new heights in their careers under Emery's management at Villa Park.

Former Scotland defender Rachel Corsie, who had a spell playing in the Women's Super League for Aston Villa late in her career, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Emery is quite unique. A lot of coaches will focus on the tactical detail, but he's so intense with it.

"I remember from when I was here that his car is always at the training ground. I know people will say that's a natural thing and the life of a manager, but I would say it's an incredible amount of time.

"He loves to get the detail right. He never gets tired of trying to better people individually and that takes an incredible amount of work. So many players come here, improve and thrive."

Jackson has prior experience of playing under Emery, having been coached by him at Villarreal, where he spent three years before Chelsea signed him for £35m.

Emery told BBC Match of the Day: "I knew him at Villarreal and he started playing the level he is now. I know his capacity to exploit his qualities and I know, as well, his humility.

"The mentality is coming through - how focused he is in life and professional career."

Speaking to TNT Sports, Jackson added: "It's not easy [to settle at a new club] but easier because of the coach and the players.

"It's an incredible dressing room with an incredible manager. I'm very happy to be here and hopefully I will score many goals."

articles.title: Stoke 0-0 Bristol City: Goalless at the bet365 Stadium
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Bristol City at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday; Mark Robins' Potters and Michael Skubala's Robins battle to a point.
articles.body:
The visitors came closest to pinching a winner through Gibson Yah's first-half effort.

Mark Robins' men have lost just once in their last nine matches, while Bristol City avoided a third straight defeat following back-to-back 1-0 losses.

The stalemate sees the Robins sit 14th in the Championship table, while Stoke drop out of the play-off places to fall to ninth.

Stoke's one enforced change saw Luca Bombino replace the in-form Eric Bocat at left wing-back after the latter suffered a knee injury in the Potters' 1-0 win over Derby last time out.

There was much more movement in the Robins line-up, with the most eyebrow-raising of Michael Skubala's four changes seeing Brad Collins, once signed by Robins at Coventry, make his competitive debut in goal in place of Sam Tickle.

Lisav Eissat, Joe Williams and Lorent Tolaj replaced Rob Atkinson, Yu Hirakawa and Scott Twine as City changed to a 3-5-2 formation to match their in-form hosts.

Only West Ham had picked up more points than the 19 Stoke had accumulated since losing their opening three games of the season, and the hosts made the brighter start at a wet and windy bet365 Stadium.

Lamine Cisse latched onto Ben Wilmot's defence-splitting pass before blazing his effort high and wide inside the opening two minutes.

Wilmot then took advantage of some indecisiveness in the Bristol City defence, nipping in and firing his effort past the far post.

Much of Stoke's early good play had come down the right between Wilmot and Cisse, but when the latter was forced off injured after 20 minutes, the hosts' threat dwindled.

The Robins took 35 minutes to notch their first attempt on goal when Dom Ballard was played in by Eissat and cut inside before firing his effort off Bosun Lawal for a corner.

The best opening of the half was to come shortly after when Bristol City wing-back Rio Cardines found space down the right and cut back for Yah, who scuffed his effort wide from 12 yards out.

Lawal then fired over following Jack McGlynn's corner.

The visitors started the second half where they left off in the first, with former Stoke loanee Luke McNally heading Cameron Pring's cross narrowly wide eight minutes after the restart.

Justin Devenny had scored two goals for the Potters since his move from Crystal Palace without getting back on the scoresheet since early September, but he came agonisingly close to putting Stoke ahead when he almost got on the end of George Hirst's knockdown following McGlynn's corner.

At the other end, Ballard glanced Pring's corner over the bar before whistling an effort narrowly over the crossbar as the visitors continued to threaten.

As the clash ticked over into stoppage time, McGlynn's curling effort left Collins stranded in the Robins' goal, but flashed past the left-hand post as both sides were left to settle for a point.

"It was really difficult. I can't be too critical and I don't want to be, because I don't think it's warranted. I think that we've tried to do everything that we could to get a goal, but I didn't think we were good enough.

"We move it in different areas and it becomes a bit samey and we don't learn from that. They've changed shape today, they've come for a difficult game and then the weather made it doubly so.

"We've tried everything but we've been in positions where we've taken a safe position to get on the ball rather than something a little bit more incisive.

"That's the only sort of slight disappointment, but when a team comes and sits like that, and it's the first time a team has come and done that, I think we've got to take some learning from it and where we've got to be positioned on the pitch.

"We had total control of the ball, total control of the game, but an easy option on it. Set plays we were dangerous, I thought it looked like we were going to score from one of them, I think we tried to negate their threat.

"To be fair to them, they've thrown bodies in front when they needed to and we didn't manage to get the winning goal, but if you can't win, don't lose."

Bristol City head coach Michael Skubala:

"A typical Championship, windy game of football. I thought it was a really good character performance from ourselves, I thought the game was difficult for both teams.

"We created some excellent moments in the game, some good box entries where we probably didn't have the last bit but I thought we came with a plan to set up and hit them on the counter-attack and I thought we did that well at times, so I'm really pleased with the performance and a good point on the road.

"We've been looking at it for a while to see if we can solidify, make ourselves stronger without the ball, but I thought the shape change was good, the lads were excellent in it and there was some really good performances.

"We knew how tough it would be because they've started the season very well here.

"They've got some really fast players on the top line, put some teams to the sword here, but I thought we defended very well and created some big chances.

"For us to defend and get our second clean sheet of the season is really important, to limit a Stoke team who have been on a really good run is also excellent, and I think we just needed to hit the target with some of our chances to turn it into a win."

articles.title: Bromley vs Peterborough
articles.summary: Bromley could not kick off the post-Andy Woodman era with a win as Vernon Masara's last-gasp leveller secured Peterborough a point from a hard-fought 1-1 draw.
articles.body:
The Ravens took the lead inside 10 minutes with Michael Cheek getting among the goals for the first time in Sky Bet League One. The frontman latched on to a loose ball in the penalty area before sweeping home.

Will Hondermarck nearly made it two moments later when his driving run drew a save from Alex Bass at his near post.

Harry Leonard should have drawn Peterborough level on the half-hour mark but the frontman placed his free header wide with only Grant Smith to beat.

Six minutes before the interval, Ethan Williams' curling effort forced Smith into a fine save low at his right-hand post.

Despite controlling possession in the second half, the Posh failed to create clear-cut opportunities.

Kamarl Grant's header 15 minutes from time went close to doubling Bromley's lead but Bass was on hand to deny him.

Substitute Nicke Kabamba missed a golden opportunity two minutes from time as Lucca Mendonca denied him with a last-gasp challenge and that proved critical when Masara rounded Smith deep into stoppage time to grab a point.

articles.title: Lincoln 4-1 Burnley: Imps thump four past sorry Clarets
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Burnley at the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday; Imps thump four in rout of Nicky Hayen's struggling Clarets side.
articles.body:
The visitors led through substitute Andreas Hountndji's strike before Ben House levelled in first-half stoppage time.

And the damage was done within eight second-half minutes as Ladefoged and Dom Jefferies ensured the Imps secured victory in the first league meeting between the two sides this century on a miserable afternoon in Lincolnshire.

Danish striker Ladefoged put the game beyond doubt with his second with just over 20 minutes to go but the writing was already on the wall.

Burnley's afternoon got even worse when George Wickens saved Marcus Edwards' penalty late on.

Both managers rung the changes in a bid to get back to winning ways and it was Tom Shaw who ended his side's winless run of four games to go seven points safe of the danger zone as Burnley remained rooted inside the dreaded bottom three.

Burnley, who were relegated from the Premier League last term, have won just one game all season and after calls from disgruntled fans for him to be dismissed, Hayen was sacked later on Saturday.

The hosts almost got off to the perfect start when Romanian international Andrei Coubis had the ball in the net inside the first five minutes, only for it rightfully to be ruled out for offside.

Lincoln's Reeco Hackett blocked Max Alleyne's effort on the line to keep the game goalless in the 25th minute.

The Clarets hit the front in the 39th minute when Hountndji, who came off the bench after 11 minutes to replace the injured Armando Broja, tapped home Lucas Pires' in-swinging corner at the back post.

But the lead didn't last long as House poked home at the back post himself after Coubis' long throw evaded everyone in the box deep in first-half stoppage time.

And Lincoln led minutes into the second half as 23-year-old Ladefoged curled an unstoppable strike from close range home with Gregoire Coudert well beaten.

Welshman Jefferies netted his first league goal since March with a strike from outside the box after Burnley failed to clear their lines from a corner.

Ladefoged made it four in the 67th minute when he headed home House's cross into the top right corner.

Ryley Towler felled Hountondji in the box, but Wickens guessed correctly to rub salt into the already gaping Clarets' wounds six minutes from time.

"I'm delighted. I'm delighted for a few groups of people… the staff and the players for the work ethic and what goes on behind the scenes that you really don't see.

"Probably more importantly than anyone is the supporters. We felt we owed them one for the West Ham experience. It's a game we wish we could have back. We owed them something.

"We felt we were a little bit short points wise for our performances here. So we knew this was a big day and a big opportunity.

"We got our reward of Lincoln City beating Burnley 4-1 in a league game.

"You've got to remember the journey and all the people that helped us get here.

"Obviously we had the West Ham experience and then Millwall away with those last 20 minutes at The Den (drawing 2-2 from 2-0 up).

"That feeling at full-time, for everybody, was amazing. It was just an amazing day and one to build on for us.

"That's what we want this football team to look like and play like.

"We've got nothing to fear when you can see what our group is capable of."

"We had one saved on the line and then scored a goal. And you think you can push on even more, but then we conceded another easy goal. A throw in went to the second post and no one takes responsibility to clear it and they react faster than us.

"It's the same story of the season for us that we keep conceding easy goals and you saw that in the second half.

"They want to work hard, but you have to show it. What we do in training is really good, but we can't execute that the same way in the games. Is that pressure? I don't know.

"It's frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn't matter because it's another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

"We haven't got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops.

"I don't know (if I will still be in charge). I know it's a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board."

articles.title: Preston 1-1 West Brom: Graham Alexander claims first point as North End boss
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and West Bromwich Albion at Deepdale on Saturday; Graham Alexander earns his first point as Lilywhites boss.
articles.body:
The Norwegian came off the bench on the hour and rifled home an 82nd-minute leveller just four minutes after Andrew Hughes hooked North End into the lead from a corner.

James Morrison's visitors had already come from behind to win against Wrexham and Blackburn in their last two matches but Preston deserved their point.

It was their first since Alexander took charge earlier this month and came at the end of a week where two of their first-team coaches left the club, in part as a result of their position at the bottom of the Championship.

Preston started well in the troublesome wet and windy conditions with Johnny Kenny forcing Max O'Leary into a low save with a speculative shot in the opening two minutes before Leo Leroy dragged an effort across goal shortly after.

West Brom were 2-0 inside 12 minutes against Blackburn last weekend and it was another slow start here, though Isaac Price did force Daniel Iversen into a smart save with a 28th-minute curling effort.

The Northern Ireland midfielder should have hit the target 12 minutes later, guiding Jayson Molumby's wind-assisted cross wide from close range.

Chances were in short supply for both teams but Alexander's side had a clear opening within 60 seconds of the second half as Kenny teed up Delano Burgzorg in the box and O'Leary did well to parry the Dutchman's powerful shot.

A few minutes later, Kenny went from provider to goal-chaser, trying to place an effort in at the near post from just inside the box, though it was a fairly routine save for Albion keeper O'Leary.

The wind was in the Lilywhites' sails and Burgzorg floundered an even better opportunity to bag the opener in the 54th minute, stabbing wide a gorgeous low delivery from Stanley Mills with the goal gaping.

Not long later, it was a chance-a-piece in quick succession as Kenny headed over Andrija Vukcevic's whipped in cross before Felix Myhre's point-blank prod was brilliantly blocked by Iversen as Brayann Pereira's header deflected perfectly into his path.

Perseverance and endeavour paid off for the hard-working home team and Hughes flicked Leroy's corner into the net with the visiting defence allowing the corner to bounce into his path.

Elation rang around three quarters of Deepdale but it was short lived as Heggebo slammed West Brom level in the 82nd minute as Preston failed to clear their lines after Iversen had brilliantly tipped Price's close-range strike on to the post.

"It's how we want to compete without a shadow of a doubt. We didn't take a backwards step. They're a really good team.

"They've got some top players who can open you up but they didn't make us go backwards and submit and just stand off them.

"We gained strength from just turning a few balls over and I think it gave the players more confidence to stay on the front foot and I think there's a risk-reward element to it."

"I thought we were in control for large periods. I felt we weren't very good in the top-end of the pitch. We weren't clinical enough. We didn't have enough spark in the top end of the pitch.

"I enjoyed watching us in some stages. I felt we were getting into lots of opportunities but without creating anything.

"There were a lot of opportunities where we could have had the opportunity to score but I felt we didn't have that in us today. I felt we took the easy options and then, when it's 0-0, they've always got an opportunity.

"The goal, obviously, we don't get them but we seem to gift goals at the moment which is worrying."

articles.standfirst: El técnico perico se encuentra en una situación delicada tras la derrota ante el Real Racing
articles.summary: El técnico perico se encuentra en una situación delicada tras la derrota ante el Real Racing
articles.body: El Espanyol ha caído en su encuentro ante el Real Racing. Los blanquiazules se adelantaban en el segundo tiempo mediante un tanto de Edu Expósito pero los locales remontaban con goles de Belocian y Zabiri en los instantes finales del duelo. Una derrota que deja al Espanyol en puestos de descenso y que deja en una situación muy complicada a su técnico. Tras el encuentro, Manolo González comparecía en rueda de prensa para tratar de explicar lo sucedido y responder a las dudas que existen sobre su futuro. Repetición del guión de partido: “Nos hacemos pequeños, no sé el motivo, los cambios eran para no echarnos para atrás, pero hemos dejado de presionar y de apretar y de tener el balón como en la primera parte. No hay otra explicación”. El árbitro no es excusa: “No quiero halar de los árbitros. No es un tema del penalti, es jun tema de que te pones por delante jugando y llagando bien en el primer tiempo. Luego, sin tocar nada, dejas de hacer todo lo que estabas haciendo. No hemos tocado nada del sistema y los cambios han sido de ataque para seguir igual, pero no hay mucha explicación. En el primer gol no salimos a tapar y en el segundo dejamos que bote 20 veces dentro del área”. Sobre el futuro del técnico: “No hablaré de ello en rueda de prensa. Es un tema privado, si el club quiere hablar nos sentaremos. No es algo para hablar aquí. La situación es delicada y lo único que podemos hacer es seguir trabajando. La valoraciones hay que hacerlas de manera interna”. “Es una situación que tendré que hablar con el club. No hay más. Es comprensible lo que pueda hacer el club. No depende de mi”. Sobre la dinámica del equipo: “La dinámica es mala. Hay momentos que son buenos y luego lo dejamos de hacer. Es como si tuviéramos miedo a perder y dejásemos de ir”. Sobre el nivel de la plantilla: “Lo que no puedo hacer es criticar ni al club ni a la plantilla, porque ni es correcto ni es la verdad. No se puede buscar excusas y decir cosas que no son verdad”. Falta de confianza del equipo: “No es un tema de intensidad, es una falta de confianza o de temor a perder lo que tienes ganado. Cuando dejas de hacerlo, le das mucha vida al equipo rival, que también es mérito de ellos”.

articles.title: La cruel lesión de Otorbi silencia Mestalla
articles.standfirst: El chaval, que debutaba como titular con Aguirre, se rompió en su primera gran arrancada y se marchó en camilla... y llorando
articles.summary: El chaval, que debutaba como titular con Aguirre, se rompió en su primera gran arrancada y se marchó en camilla... y llorando
articles.body: Un jugador se llevó la mayor ovación del equipo cuando desde megafonía se anunció el once titular del Valencia para el derbi ante el Villarreal. David Otorbi se estrenaba como titular con Aguirre después de dos partidos en los que saliendo desde el banquillo había sido el mejor del equipo. Todo estaba dispuesto para que el canterano de 19 años se convirtiera en el protagonista del partido. Era su momento... y todo se vino abajo. En la primera gran arrancada en velocidad al espacio, su característica más destacada, el joven extremo se lanzó al suelo y el grito silenció Mestalla. Sólo se habían jugado 11 minutos. Mano a la parte de atrás del muslo derecho y sensación de haberse roto por completo. El estadio no se lo podía creer. La cosa fue a más cuando el chico no pudo ni dar un paso y tuvo que ser retirado en camilla mientras se tapaba el rostro lleno de lágrimas. Una desgracia que corta de raíz la explosión del joven que había ilusionado a la grada del estadio. La gente se dio cuenta de la gravedad de la cosa y coreó el nombre del canterano mientras se retiraba en medio de una sonora ovación. La lesión de Otorbi se une a la plaga que azotó al equipo durante el mes de septiembre y que ha mandado a demasiados jugadores a la enfermería. A falta de pruebas, da la sensación de que Otorbi estará bastante tiempo alejado de los terrenos de juego.

articles.title: Cardiff 1-0 Birmingham: Yousef Salech steers Bluebirds to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Birmingham City at the Cardiff City Stadium on Saturday; Yousef Salech misses penalty but then scores winner.
articles.body:
Salech was named among the home substitutes initially, but defender Krystian Bielik suffered an injury in the warm-up and had to drop out on an afternoon of relentless rain in the Welsh capital.

The late change saw Cardiff reshuffle their resources and Salech plunder a first-half winner, his sixth goal of the season coming 10 minutes after James Beadle had saved his spot-kick.

Cardiff have now recorded three straight home wins as they continue to show real signs of adapting to life in the second tier following promotion from League One.

Birmingham had arrived on the back of three successive wins without conceding, and remain in the play-off places after suffering their first defeat since September 9.

Cardiff manager Brian Barry-Murphy was serving a touchline ban after receiving his third yellow card of the season.

Both sets of players wore black armbands to mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster, in which 116 children were among the 144 who died in the Welsh mining village, and a minute's silence before kick-off was impeccably observed.

Salech featured for the first time in five weeks after a shoulder injury, but could not pull down a Joel Bagan pass that would have taken him through on goal.

Luis Vazquez's wait for a first Birmingham goal went on as the Argentinian striker was unable to connect with Jay Stansfield's cross.

Cardiff were awarded a spot-kick after 21 minutes when Tomoki Iwata dragged down Perry Ng at a corner. Salech sent the penalty low to Beadle's right, but the effort lacked power and the Birmingham goalkeeper pushed the ball to safety.

It was the second successive spot-kick Cardiff had missed following Chris Willock's failure to convert against Watford.

But Salech quickly made amends by holding off Phil Neumann from Ollie Tanner's cross and producing a tidy turn and finish past Beadle.

Some Birmingham players held their arms aloft believing Neumann had been sent to the floor by a foul, but referee Tim Robinson clearly saw it as a case of Salech being stronger.

Beadle came to Birmingham's rescue at the start of the second half, denying Cian Ashford with his legs after Tanner and Salech had opened up the visitors.

Salech fired just past the base of a post as Cardiff increased intensity in the search for a second goal and Beadle fielded Ashford's attempt from distance.

Birmingham had not tested Nathan Trott until Stansfield met Alex Cochrane's cross, but it was a routine stop to say the least and Cardiff were untroubled until the closing stages.

Marvin Ducksch headed Max Bird's cross wide and Birmingham's best chance came two minutes from time when Trott superbly kept out Demarai Gray from point-blank range.

"We understood what the day meant to everybody, so to get the victory that was so badly wanted is very special for everyone. It was very important for the players to watch the footage we saw, and to understand what the people there have been through.

"I think we're at our best when we're playing a very intense type of football.

"Sometimes we're good enough to win and sometimes we're not, but that's what we're always striving for, to play that type of aggressive, front-footed performance."

"The best team won, in any game if you're second to the ball that much it's always going to be hard.

"Every time we had possession of the ball there was a blue shirt on us. They are a side who do put the press on and we just couldn't get close to their box.

"We were very disorganised for the goal, how easy it came in to the box and the goal. That's unlike us. We gave ourselves a big job to recover from that and we expected more."

articles.title: Blackburn 2-0 Wrexham: Andri Gudjohnsen double steers Rovers to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Blackburn Rovers and Wrexham at Ewood Park on Saturday; Andri Gudjohnsen double steers Rovers to victory against the Red Dragons.
articles.body:
The Icelandic striker's return from injury has coincided with an upturn in Rovers' results as goals in each half delivered a third win in five games that moves Tony Mowbray's side to within two points of the play-offs.

His first, a minute before half-time, was a poacher's finish as he swept in when Sam Morsy's shot was parried, and he made the game safe in the 79th minute with an emphatic strike from 12 yards for his eighth of the campaign.

It could have been more comfortable as Dapo Afolayan and Augustus Kargbo went close, and although Sam Smith headed wide for Wrexham with the score at 1-0, Phil Parkinson's men were outclassed as their winless away run stretched to four.

Rovers were a whisker away from hitting the front in the third minute when Jayden Fevrier cut in from the right and curled agonisingly wide of the far post.

Wrexham settled into the game with both Kieffer Moore and Callum O'Hare's shots blocked in the 14th minute as Rovers desperately tried to clear their lines.

Mowbray's men weathered that pressure and nearly gave the visitors a taste of their own medicine when Hayden Carter's outstretched foot diverted Todd Cantwell's 42nd-minute corner goalwards, only for the ball to strike the post before Anthony Patterson gratefully gathered.

There was no reprieve two minutes later when Moussa Baradji, making his first start of the season, wriggled away from two players and set up Sam Morsy, whose long-range effort was parried by Patterson straight to Gudjohnsen, who clinically swept into the bottom right corner.

Afolayan missed a glorious chance to double the advantage four minutes after the restart when Cantwell's pass sent him through one-on-one but Patterson spread himself brilliantly to repel the effort.

Wrexham started to create chances of their own as Matty James volleyed wide before O'Hare's 57th-minute cross found Smith, who glanced a free header wide of the far post.

They went close again 10 minutes later when Jacques Ekomie raided down the left and crossed for Moore, whose left-foot shot was blocked and fell to Joe Worrall, who hammered just wide of the left post from inside the area.

Rovers introduced Kargbo from the bench and his express pace almost brought a counter-attacking second as he burst forward from a Wrexham corner on to Cantwell's pass and drove low from the right, forcing Patterson to parry behind.

However, Gudjohnsen made the game safe 11 minutes from time with another deadly finish, latching on to Cantwell's pass 12 yards out before turning away from Worrall and burying into the top corner.

"Andri has started his career pretty well, I think, and it goes where it goes, hopefully with us trying to fire the goals for a season or two.

"People tell me he was scoring a lot of goals at the start of the last season and then he picked up an injury. So he's obviously very, very talented.

"He's got good movement, he strikes a brilliant ball, he's very physical and competitive. He's got all the attributes.

"I've just talked about humility in the dressing room and as long as he carries that with him everywhere, he's got a great chance to have a wonderful career.

"He's a great kid, nice lad, doesn't get carried away with anything. I can feel the steadiness of him, he's just scored quite a lot of goals, even before today. And there's no overconfident guy. He just gets on with his job. He's very humble and I like him a lot."

"Difficult conditions for both sides. We were against it a bit in terms of elements first half.

"Obviously conceding just before the break was a setback but we still felt at half-time the game was there for us. But we couldn't produce the quality we needed.

"We've had 23 attempts but to only have one of those on target, we have to look at that.

"I've got to give Blackburn defenders credit because they blocked things, made 9-10 blocks. They defended crosses, they defended set plays. It was a combination of their good defending, but we couldn't find that clinical moment to get us back in the game and the game was separated on two moments.

"When we analyse the positions we got into, we got in enough good positions to have got something from the game but we just didn't produce the quality."

articles.title: Celta - Betis | Gallegos y andaluces se tocan la moral
articles.standfirst: Gallegos y andaluces llegan a este gran choque con la moral por las nubes después sus respectivas victorias esta semana en Europa
articles.summary: Gallegos y andaluces llegan a este gran choque con la moral por las nubes después sus respectivas victorias esta semana en Europa
articles.body: Celta y Betis se citan en Balaídos en un choque que medirá sus subidas de moral tras ganar en Europa. Los gallegos ganaron al Celtic y llevan seis jornadas sin perder, pero enfrente tendrán a un Betis que ganó al Feyenoord en Champions, zona que ocupan en estos momentos en la tabla liguera. Olvidada la goleada del Barça, los de Pellegrini quieren aprovechar el cansancio y las numerosas bajas de los de Vigo en un duelo que promete ser muy ofensivo y con muchos goles. Con el cansancio de un largo retorno desde Glasgow, por complicaciones en el vuelo, afronta el Celta un partido en el que busca encadenar su tercera victoria de la semana y a su vez tercera consecutiva en Balaídos, algo que solo consiguió en una ocasión la pasada temporada. El técnico convocó a todos sus jugadores disponibles ante la media decena de bajas con las que, por lesión, no pueden participar en el partido. Con mucha ausencia pero con la moral por las nubes tras la sensacional victoria ante el Celtic que ha supuesto una gran inyección de moral para los de Vigo. Después de conseguir el histórico tres de tres en victorias en la Champions League, a los verdiblancos les toca revertir la derrota que sufrió ante el Barcelona en LaLiga para mantenerse en una posición privilegiada en plena vorágine de partidos entre parones. Manuel Pellegrini rotará una vez más. No podrá contar con el sancionado Facundo Bernal. El uruguayo cumplirá en Balaídos su primer partido de sanción de los cuatro que deberá cumplir tras su encontronazo con Lamine Yamal. Por lesión pierde a Junior y a Cucho Hernández. Pablo Durán vs Parrott. El duelo de pistoleros en Balaídos puede ser de lo más destacado del encuentro. Ambos llegan con mucho hambre de gol y en ellos caerá la máxima responsabilidad de llevarse los tres puntos. El Celta tiene una de las visitas más complicadas porque el Betis es uno de los equipos más en forma en este arranque liguero. Ambos llegan de ganar en Europa, pero los de Pellegrini con un día más de descanso y los de Giráldez, además, con los problemas de su regreso a Vigo.

articles.title: Vitor Matos says Swansea City mujst 'listen to performance' after QPR thrashing
articles.summary: Vitor Matos says Swansea City must "listen to this performance" after they slump to the heaviest defeat of his reign at Queens Park Rangers.
articles.body:
Vitor Matos says Swansea City must "listen to this performance" after they slumped to the heaviest defeat of his reign at Queens Park Rangers.

Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes to help Rangers claim a remarkable 5-0 victory over Matos' high-flying Swansea side.

The Swans remain in the Championship's automatic promotion places despite their dismal afternoon at Loftus Road.

Head coach Matos says he takes responsibility for the QPR thrashing, but says all at Swansea must learn lessons from painful defeat.

"It's up to us to improve and it's up to us to go back to our standards, to bounce back from the situation we are in at the moment," Matos told BBC Sport Wales.

"We were not perfect when we were winning.

"The performance does not erase what we have done, but we need to listen to this game, we need to listen to this performance and understand what we need to do much better."

Swansea had lost only two of their 11 league games this season before taking on a Rangers side who had won only one of their previous seven matches.

But Swansea's familiar resilience was nowhere to be seen as Kone's treble and two set-piece goals from centre-back Jimmy Dunne gave QPR a resounding victory.

Matos' previous heaviest losses as Swansea boss were 3-0 defeats to Coventry and Ipswich last season, while this was the club's worst league result since a 5-0 mauling at Southampton in December 2023.

"Queens Park Rangers started with a lot of energy, [while] we lacked concentration and organisation in moments," Matos added.

"They were really clinical in their finishing and that didn't give us the confidence we need. In the end it's my responsibility.

"It's up to me to put the team on the pitch, to improve the team. And that's what we need to do now – to understand, to analyse and improve again."

Matos, meanwhile, revealed Swansea have suffered another injury blow after Moussa Yeo was missing at QPR.

The in-form winger suffered a hamstring problem during last weekend's defeat by West Ham United which means he will be sidelined for between two and three weeks.

"Of course losing Moussa is not the best for us, but we have a strong squad and we will find a way to cover his absence," Matos said.

News of Yeo's injury comes after fellow wideman Ronald was ruled out for up to eight weeks with a hamstring injury.

Another winger, Jeremy Monga, was part of Swansea's matchday squad on Saturday for the first time since joining on loan from Manchester City, though the teenager did not make it on to the pitch.

articles.title: Indian Super League: Ajaraie misses last-gasp penalty as Odisha hold NEUFC
articles.summary: KOLKATA: It was almost an encore of their Indian Super League opener as NorthEast United once again looked set for a very late win on Saturday as Odisha
articles.body: KOLKATA: It was almost an encore of their Indian Super League opener as NorthEast United once again looked set for a very late win on Saturday as Odisha FC defender Stephen Eze conceded a penalty in the fifth minute of injury time.However, contrary to expectations, Alaaeddine Ajaraie’s spot kick beat goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwary but not the woodwork as the match at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar ended in a goalless draw.It was, in fact, a fair result for the eighth-paced Juggernauts, who got their first point of the season, and their impressive defence, as the Highlanders failed to continue their winning run even as the point took them to the top of the table with seven points from three matches.The match began as a tactical battle between the coaches with TS Purushothaman resorting to a strong defensive shape that the hosts have been more used to over the seasons, with three centre-backs – Jeremy Zohminghlua, veteran Eze and Thoiba Singh Moirangthem – inside the six-yard box.It was a perfect answer to Juan Pedro Benali’s tactic of quick attack with Ajaraie in a more central role in combination with Nikola Ninkovic and aided by Jithin MS and Macarton Nickson from the wings.Jithin, who scored the winner in their opener against the mighty Mohun Bagan Super Giant, created the first NEUFC attack as early as in the third minute with a run from the right wing and beating a persistent Jeremy to send in a ball at the centre. But Odisha’s young custodian Hrithik Tiwary stood tall to parry the shot from Ninkovic towards safety.Ajaraie, away from his conventional position in the flanks, made a few impressive runs throughout the first half, especially in the 23rd and 28th minutes, down the middle, but after dodging and nutmegging the defenders, failed to produce the finish that his Spanish coach hoped for from the sidelines.Odisha, on the other hand, depended on counter-attacks as Everton Nascimento, Mahmoud Eid and K Lalrinfela waited in the opposition half to find a breakthrough.The best chance of the half came to Antonio Moyano in the 45th minute but, with only Tiwary to beat, he shot the ball too high to make a difference.Although devoid of a goal, the match continued to be an exciting affair with a proactive Jithin and skilful Ajaraie used all tricks in their bag to get past the Odisha defence. There were also physical duels, like the ones involving the young Blue Tigers and Highlanders attacker Pramveer Singh and Odisha skipper Lalthathanga Khawlhring or ‘Putieia’ in the middle.However, the scoreline stayed unchanged even as the ends were changed and both coaches brought in reinforcements.Even as the NEUFC attacks continued, with Ajaraie and Ninkovic coming very close to scoring throughout the second half, Everton and Eid combined near the NEUFC goal with some impressive moves, together with substitute Rahim Ali, only for the hard-working Nikhil Barla at the back and Gurmeet Singh in goal coming to NEUFC’s rescue.That was until the 95th minute of the match when all the hard work from Odisha looked to have been put paid by the outstretched hand of Eze inside the box.However, it was not to be as the right post saved Ajaraie’s penalty kick and Odisha’s day in front of the home crowd.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Lo de Matarazzo buscan su cuarto triunfo seguido ante un Levante que llega crecido a Anoeta
articles.body: La Real Sociedad recibirá esta tarde al Levante en Anoeta con la intención de sumar su cuarta victoria seguida en LaLiga y mantenerse en los puestos europeos, a los que soñarán con acercarse los granotas, algo que podrían hacer si dan continuidad al triunfo del miércoles contra el Athletic y se llevan los tres puntos. Ambos equipos están protagonizando partidos con goles, así que todo apunta a tarde entretenida. La Real está atravesando por uno de sus mejores momentos cara a gol de los últimos años, como lo prueban el 2-5 en Málaga y el 0-6 en Noruega, además de los tres tantos que hizo ante Dépor, Valencia o Elche, así que la idea será mantener esa línea y sumar tres puntos con los que afianzarse en la quinta posición y seguir aumentando hueco con los rivales en la pelea por Europa. Matarazzo ha venido realizando muchos cambios en su equipo titular, pero hoy podría no hacer muchas variaciones con el respecto al jueves. Remiro volverá a la portería, veremos si Fort a la defensa y Turrientes al doble pivote, con Barrenetxea siendo de la partida en un ataque con la duda de Óskarsson. Aramburu y Herrera volvieron, pero parece pronto para que sean de la partida. El Levante buscará la segunda victoria consecutiva y encadenar el cuarto envite seguido sin car derrotado, tras el triunfo ante el Athletic Club y los empates ante el Sevilla y Deportivo de A Coruña. En una tranquila undécima posición, los granotas no se situaban tan altos en la tabla desde abril de 2021, cuando en el cierre de la trigésima segunda jornada acumulaban 38 puntos para acariciar la permanencia que finalmente alcanzaron. Para este choque, Luís Castro sigue recuperando efectivos en su lista de disponibles. Tras el regreso, con gol incluido de Etta Eyong, este fin de semana se suma Hugo Sotelo, que ha conseguido superar su lesión muscular y podrá tener sus primeros minutos. Sin embargo, seguirá teniendo en la enfermería a Dela que sigue arrastrando molestias musculares y Bardeli, que causa baja por lesión. Oyarzabal vs. Iván Romero. Los hombres gol, los referentes ofensivos de sus equipos —2 y 3 dianas cada uno hasta ahora en Liga— y sobre los que muchos ojos se fijarán esta tarde en Donosti.

articles.title: Nicky Hayen: Burnley head coach sacked after just 14 games
articles.summary: Nicky Hayen is sacked after just 14 games in charge at Burnley following a poor start to the season.
articles.body:
Head coach Nicky Hayen has been sacked after just 14 games in charge at Burnley following a poor start to the season.

Hayen's final match was Saturday's 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City , as the hosts came back from 1-0 down to emphatically condemn the Clarets to a sixth defeat of the campaign and leave them 22nd in the Championship.

Belgian Hayen was only appointed on 10 July to succeed Scott Parker, who left at the end of April days after the Clarets' relegation from the Premier League was confirmed.

Burnley announced the news with a short two-sentence statement within two hours of their defeat at the ProAmpac Stadium.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Hayen had said: "I'm not going to lose my energy because this is something out of my hands" with reference to his future.

Hayen won the Belgian title with Club Brugge in 2024 and was brought in by owner Alan Pace to oversee a promotion bid, with the Clarets having gone up in their last two Championship campaigns in 2023 and 2025.

But after a promising draw with West Ham on the opening weekend, their season has nosedived and the club are without a win at home in the league since beating Leeds United at Turf Moor in the Premier League over a year ago.

The Clarets earned a first win of the season in style earlier this month as they returned from the extended international break to beat struggling Watford 4-0 but then drew against Charlton and lost to Wolves, scoring first in both matches.

Saturday's defeat to the Imps also means they have won just one of the past 24 league games and have conceded 25 goals from their opening 12 Championship games - the worst record in the division.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal boss keeping tabs on Premier League managers leaving the technical area
articles.summary: Wandering Premier League managers beware, Arsenal's Mikel Arteta has compiled a dossier of bosses leaving their technical area.
articles.body:
Wandering Premier League managers beware, Mikel Arteta has the receipts.

The Arsenal boss has developed a reputation for straying outside the technical area in recent years but, he claims, he is far from the worst offender.

After receiving his second yellow card of the season for the offence during the Gunners' victory over Everton on Saturday, Arteta revealed he has a dossier of evidence that proves other Premier League managers are getting off lightly.

"I do have to be careful. They should put sensors there," he said.

"There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline - no yellows.

"I am clipping all of that so I have now a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me I can say, 'I am not in the record yet'. Somebody else has the record so let's see.

"Then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don't know what we are going to do - let's see."

What is Arteta planning to do with this treasure trove of touchline images? Who is the mystery manager holding that surely unbreakable record?

For now we can only speculate, although a BBC Sport study in April 2025 found that of current top-flight bosses, Aston Villa 's Unai Emery spent the most time outside his technical area. Could he be the culprit?

Until all is revealed, though, Premier League bosses must watch their step - Arteta is watching.
