articles.title: Falkirk 3-0 Kilmarnock: Jacob Murrell strikes as Falkirk cruise past Kilmarnock amid stormy conditions
articles.summary: Report as Falkirk move up to seventh in the Scottish Premiership table with a 3-0 win at home to Kilmarnock
articles.body:
Visiting centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger converted past Calum Ferrie either side of a Jacob Murrell header.

Following a tough start to the campaign, John McGlynn's men have lost just one of their last six games.

It was clear from an early stage that the side who coped best amid torrid conditions would prosper.

That team was emphatically Falkirk, with focal point forward Murrell netting his fifth league goal of the season.

Neither side gained a level of control over the ball, never mind the game as a whole, for much of the first half but the Bairns adapted better.

A wild wind was firmly against the visitors in that 45, making for a fraught opening spell.

Leon McCann's deep cross was blown towards the top corner, forcing Ferrie into emergency action to tip the ball over the crossbar.

The Kilmarnock goalkeeper's kicks barely made it 35 yards.

Owen Eames skewed wide with the first decent chance as Falkirk began to stretch the game midway through the half.

They opened Killie up down the right to seize a 29th-minute lead. Ethan Ross conjured a terrific deep delivery to pick out Murrell at the back post.

The American did not muster much power behind his header and it looked bound for Ferrie's arms. However, on-loan Hull defender McCarthy needlessly thrust out a knee to connect and beat his own keeper.

Kilmarnock came within inches of a swift reply when a Tom Lowery cross was diverted onto the bar and went over.

Falkirk remained well on top, however, and doubled the lead seven minutes before the break.

Ferrie batted away a Ross drive at his near post to concede a corner. Ryan Strain's delivery found Murrell evading the attention of Erik Ring to flash a header off the underside of the bar and in.

Torrential rain added to the treacherous conditions as Falkirk rode out a period of early second-half pressure to take change once again.

Liam Henderson headed across goal from Brad Spencer's cross. Murrell could not make a clean connection with the overhead attempt and Ferrie scooped up.

Within a minute of Neil McCann bringing on Mark O'Hara and Nicky Clescenco to provide a spark, all hope of a comeback was extinguished. Stanger's attempted clearance of a Deniss Melniks header from a Falkirk free-kick gave Ferrie no chance.

The Killie keeper made fine stops from Eames and Murrell to keep the score down. And the visitors passed up their one chance for a consolation. With Scott Bain committed well out of his goal, Ieuan Owen missed the empty goal from 30 yards.

"We played the conditions - it's what you have to do and we make no excuses for that.

"But there were a lot of really good individual performances in our team. Finley Barbrook was excellent in a different position. Big Deniss (Melniks) came into midfield and did so well and Jacob (Murrell) got another goal.

"Jacob is very confident now. Like everything else, you come from America and you've got to adjust.

"Loads of things are different, even driving on the other side of the road is something you've got to get used to.

"He's living in Glasgow, he's now settled down, he's comfortable and his form is really, really good. A couple of goals last week, another one today.

"He takes the header really well. It's a carbon copy of the goal he scored at Tannadice from a corner. From my point of view, long may that last."

"It's just a horrible game of football. The conditions were absolutely terrible for both teams.

"But the bottom line is Falkirk did the ugly side of the game and the basics better to get the reward of three points. We, of course, wanted to get the ball on the deck.

"But today wasn't about getting the ball on the deck.

"I said that to them before the game. It's not, 'forget everything we've worked on' - it's just playing the conditions.

"I'm fully aware of that. I'm an experienced guy in football. I understand that you can't be a purist out there."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Jesé permite que la UD se reencuentre con las victorias
articles.standfirst: Su tempranero gol le permite volver a ganar seis jornadas después en un partido en el que los palos impidieron hasta cinco tantos más
articles.summary: Su tempranero gol le permite volver a ganar seis jornadas después en un partido en el que los palos impidieron hasta cinco tantos más
articles.body: Las Palmas pone punto final a cinco jornadas sin conocer la victoria gracias a un gol tempranero de Jesé y se reencuentra con las alegrías al doblegar a la Real Sociedad B en el Gran Canaria en una tarde en la que los palos se empeñaron en robarle protagonismo al marcador, ya que hasta en cinco ocasiones los largueros y los postes fueron protagonistas. El conjunto amarillo, que pudo ganar por una amplia ventaja, resistió las acometidas del Sanse, que volvió a quedarse sin premio y encadenó su sexta derrota consecutiva y seguirá una semana más en descenso. Los amarillos saltaron al césped con una premisa clara: que el reloj no jugara en su contra ni alimentara el recuerdo de una racha demasiado amarga. Apenas habían transcurrido ocho minutos cuando Jesé encontró un balón sin dueño en el área, tras una buena internada de Pezzolesi, y lo convirtió en gol con un disparo inapelable ajustado al poste. Sergio Viera, la sorpresa en el once local, pudo ampliar la ventaja, pero su remate se estrelló contra el larguero, primer aviso de una tarde en la que la madera acabaría por convertirse en protagonista. Y es que el Sanse también encontró en el poste un obstáculo para sus aspiraciones, ya que Dani Díaz mandó un zurdazo al larguero y Carrera un remate al poste, antes de que Caro firmara la parada del encuentro ante Gorosabel. Y, como si el destino quisiera reservarse la última palabra, el larguero volvió a cruzarse entre Manu Fuster y el gol: su vaselina superó a Olasagasti y llegó a celebrarse en la grada, pero terminó muriendo en el hierro. Con dos de las defensas más permisivas del campeonato frente a frente, resultaba difícil explicar que el descanso llegara con un único tanto en el marcador, entre otras cosas porque Olasagasti sacó metiendo una gran mano un remate de Fuster, lo mismo que hizo ante el cabezazo de Álex Suárez en el córner posterior. Entre medias le fue anulado un gol a Aguirre por un fuera de juego claro. En la reanudación, con un doble cambio en las filas realistas, uno de los recién ingresados, Astiazaran, estuvo a punto de culminar una gran internada de Dani Díaz, pero su remate desde cerca lo taponó Álex Suárez. Siguió insistiendo el filial por medio de un gran Dani Díaz, pero su gran centro lo cabeceó fuera por poco Astiazaran. Juan Manuel Rodríguez también movió el banquillo con la intención de reforzar el dominio, dando entrada a Kirian y Acimovic, mientras buscaba en Elías Romero una nueva vía para encontrar la sentencia. El recién incorporado estuvo cerca de lograrla, pero Kita le cerró el camino hacia la red lanzándose al suelo cuando Olasagasti ya parecía vencido. A partir de ahí, Caro vivió el resto del partido más tranquilo, mientras la UD aguardaba el momento de cerrar el partido. Jesé tuvo la oportunidad de hacerlo, pero su remate salió rozando el poste, y Pezzolesi también acarició el gol, pero el potente remate del lateral casi sin ángulo se topó, una vez más, con el poste. La madera se empeñó en prolongar la incertidumbre, aunque esta vez no pudo arrebatarle a Las Palmas el desenlace que necesitaba. Seis jornadas después, los amarillos volvieron a ganar y encontraron en los tres puntos una bocanada de aire para aliviar la presión.

articles.title: El Girona sentencia en tres minutos y 'saca' al Fortuna del partido para hacerle una 'manita'
articles.standfirst: El filial del Celta jugó con 10 desde el 28' por la roja directa a Meixús en un partido donde Vanat marcó tres goles
articles.summary: El filial del Celta jugó con 10 desde el 28' por la roja directa a Meixús en un partido donde Vanat marcó tres goles
articles.body: El Girona superó y goleo a un Celta Fortuna que no pudo ni supo como parar el vendaval ofensivo blanquirrojo. Vanat avanzó a los suyos poco después del primer cuarto de hora y 22 minutos después, el resultado ya era favorable a los de Quique Álvarez por 4-0 con dianas de Unai, otro más de Vanat y Carles Pérez. Con un jugador menos desde el 29, el filial del Celta intentó no salir todavía más escaldado de Montilivi en un segundo tiempo en el cual se bajaron las revoluciones, pero Vanat, con un hat-trick hizo la manita y Óscar Marcos el gol del honor visitante. La primera parte del Girona fue brutal a lo que efectividad se refiere. Los catalanes interpretaron muy bien cuando presionar y de que manera a un rival que desde el principio se vio superado por la intensidad de los locales. Y a partir del primer cuarto de hora cayeron los goles a cántaros. Abrió la lata Vanat cazando un rebote con suerte después de un intento de remate de Unai (17’). El ucraniano se convertiría en asistente del media punta gracias a un mal rechace de Meixús a un pase largo. Vanat vio bien Unai al espacio, que batió a un Coke que no se atrevió a salir bajo palos (20’). El festival catalán siguió cuando Vanat se internó en el área y recibió un empujón de Meixús. En primera instancia Guzmán Mansilla no pitó penalti pero el VAR le aconsejó acercarse al monitor ante una carga ilegal y poco vistosa que acabó con el central expulsado. El internacional con Ucrania ejecutó desde los once metros para hacer el 3-0. Antes del descanso, Carlos Pérez rubricó el primer acto con un trallazo desde la frontal que se coló por la cruceta derecha del Coke. Brutal. En el segundo acto el nivel de efectividad gerundense bajó por suerte de un Celta que juntó líneas para no lastimarse. Carles Pérez rondó la manita con un par de llegadas y disparos interesantes y Mateu Morey impactó con la parte exterior del poste izquierdo de Coke (54’), en el preludio de la manita, cuando el de Petra vio el desmarque de Vanat y el ucraniano con remate cruzado con el interior de la zurda batió al portero para hacer su hat-trick particular (55’). En un error de concentración de los catalanes, Óscar Marcos pudo hacer el gol del honor para el Celta Fortuna (59’), que dio gracias a que las llegadas blanquirrojas no fueron tan claras en el tramo final.

articles.title: Penders error, Palmer sent off - player ratings for Chelsea v Spurs
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Mike Penders endures a difficult first Premier League start, scoring an own goal in Spurs' 2-0 win at Chelsea. Here's how we - and you - rated the players.
articles.body:
Goalkeeper Mike Penders endured a difficult first Premier League start, scoring an own goal as Chelsea lost 2-0 at home to Tottenham , the 21-year-old punching the ball into his own net.

Cole Palmer was then sent off before winger Mathys Tel sealed victory with a spectacular dribble and finish in the 87th minute, as Spurs won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in 42 visits.

Here's how I rated the players, and how you rated the players.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Mike Penders : Assured was the word for the 21-year-old goalkeeper on his first start in place of the injured Emiliano Martinez. That was until a cross came in and he calamitously punched a corner into his own net, before letting in Tel's strike at his near post. 4

Josh Acheampong : Having started seven of Chelsea 's 10 games in all competitions this season, Acheampong is emerging as a reliable member of the backline. Defended well and seldom looked troubled. 6

Maxence Lacroix : The France international made several important interventions during spells when Chelsea were under pressure. 6

Levi Colwill : Colwill looked at his physical best as part of an increasingly settled backline. 6

Pedro Neto : Arguably Chelsea 's standout performer. Excellent defensively, winning the ball back high up the pitch on several occasions, while also posing a threat going forward. Saw a well-struck effort saved in the second half. 7

Moises Caicedo : Like Neto, one of Chelsea 's best performers. Constantly won possession and disrupted Tottenham 's rhythm, particularly through his battles with James Maddison before the midfielder was forced off. 8

Jordan Henderson : Should perhaps have made more of Chelsea 's best first-half chance in the 36th minute, but otherwise carried out his responsibilities effectively in midfield. 6

Jorrel Hato : A quiet evening in which he appeared more focused on containing Mohammed Kudus than supporting attacks. Taken off in the 65th minute. 5

Cole Palmer : Contributed well defensively and in Chelsea 's press. Tested Kinsky with a curling effort and was involved in several promising moves, but could not provide a decisive moment. Palmer was sent off for a late tackle on Gallagher, having been booked for causing a flashpoint by pushing over Fernandes, in nine minutes of ill-discipline. 4

Geovany Quenda : Making his first Chelsea start in place of Joao Pedro, Quenda began on the left wing and won an early free-kick. However, he struggled to make a significant attacking impact and was taken off in the 72nd minute. 6

Morgan Rogers : Looked less effective operating as a striker but still combined well with Palmer and forced a good save. Like Palmer and Quenda, he lacked the decisive touch in the final third. 6

Marco Palestra (on 65, Hato): The wing-back was involved in the physical battle. 6

Estevao Willian (on 72, Quenda): Immediately made an impact by hitting a shot into the side-netting. 6

Subs not used: Sharman-Lowe, Fofana, Gusto, Nicoll-Jazuli, Barco, Lavia, Welbeck

Antonin Kinsky : Two poor kicks put his side under pressure in the first half and he almost let a Rogers shot slip through his grasp in the rain, but got away with it. 5

Archie Gray : A solid performance without catching the eye, although the midfielder-turned-defender kept Quenda quiet for much of the game. 6

Jan-Paul van Hecke : Particularly assured on the ball despite the difficult conditions, bringing composure to those around him in defence. The big defender put pressure on Penders for the goal. 7

Micky van de Ven : Equally impressive in possession and the most adventurous member of the backline when carrying the ball forward. 7

Andy Robertson : On his 300th Premier League start, the Scotland full-back looked shaky early on but grew into the game and made an impact at both ends of the pitch. 7

Mateus Fernandes : Gave the ball away in a dangerous area for Chelsea 's first effort on goal, but deserves credit for his work as the deepest midfielder in a controlled away performance against top-six opposition. His corner led to the goal. 7

Sandro Tonali : Blazed a long-range effort over the bar late in the first half and was steady without ever truly influencing the contest. 6

James Maddison : Struggled to impose himself in the number 10 role in a fast-paced encounter and found it difficult to shake off the attentions of an aggressive Caicedo. His evening ended with injury in the 51st minute. 5

Mohammed Kudus : The Ghana winger curled a good effort wide in the first half and linked play effectively in attack. 6

Omar Marmoush : The Egypt forward squandered a good opportunity in the 29th minute with a mis-kick. More generally, he looked indecisive in the final third. 5

Mathys Tel : Scored a wondergoal for his first Premier League goal of the season to seal victory against 10-man Spurs . He had played well in the run-up to the big moment. 8

Conor Gallagher (on 51, Maddison): Added a competitive edge to the midfield in his time on the pitch, involved in Palmer being sent off, a good impact from the bench. 7

Dominic Solanke (on 65, Marmoush): Stretched Chelsea with his ability to run in behind the defence. 6

Pedro Porro (on 65, Gray): A quiet outing on his return from a hamstring injury. 6

Subs not used: Dubravka, Senesi, Davies, Olusesi, Kulusevski, Williams-Barnett

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: El Tottenham 'cala' a la 'Xabineta'
articles.standfirst: Un error de Penders a la salida de un córner y la posterior expulsión de Palmer condenan a los 'blues' · Los 'spurs' vuelven a ganar en el Bridge por primera vez desde 2018
articles.summary: Un error de Penders a la salida de un córner y la posterior expulsión de Palmer condenan a los 'blues' · Los 'spurs' vuelven a ganar en el Bridge por primera vez desde 2018
articles.body: Las victorias contra Bournemouth y Everton habían 'lanzado' al Chelsea a la vuelta del parón. Buscaban enlazar la tercera... pero la 'Xabineta' se caló ante un Tottenham (0-2) que no ganaba en Stamford Bridge desde abril de 2018. Los 'spurs', de este modo, hacen 'click' y le dan continuidad al triunfo frente al Coventry tras no lograr ganar en las seis primeras jornadas. Penders, que ya tuvo que salir por la aparatosa lesión del 'Dibu' la semana pasada, se ubicó bajo palos en un Chelsea donde Hato le ganó la partida a Chavarría en el carril zurdo y Quenda formó tridente con Rogers y Palmer por la baja de Joao Pedro a última hora. De Zerbi, sin Adarabioyo, no pudo la línea de tres propuesta ante el Coventry. Mateus Fernandes entró en la medular y Tel desplazó a Marmoush al '9'. Arrancó el choque con un ritmo electrizante. El balón viajaba con rapidez de lado a lado del campo. Fue Palmer, tras un robo alto de Pedro Neto, quien se apuntó la primera ocasión con un remate desde el lateral del área que obligó a 'volar' a Kinsky. Kudus, acto seguido, replicó con un remate calcado... que Penders siguió con la mirada. Se marchó rozando la madera. Le sirvió al Tottenham para crecer e inclinar el campo sobre la portería de un Mike Penders que entró en calor con el tibio remate de Marmoush desde el corazón del área en el 22' tras una brillante acción por izquierda entre Robertson y un Mathys Tel que, poco después, no pudo superar al belga mano a mano. Trató de entonarse el Chelsea antes del descanso y forzó a Kinsky a elevar su volumen de intervenciones. La segunda parte no pudo arrancar peor para el Tottenham por la lesión de Maddison. Tuvo que entrar Gallagher, entre pitos, para ocupar su lugar en la mediapunta. Lo trató de aprovechar el Chelsea y, por medio de Neto, volvió a probar a Kinsky en una de sus primeras salidas. Movió ficha Xabi Alonso poniendo piernas frescas sobre el césped: entraron Palestra y un Estevao que mandó un disparo al lateral de la red en su primera intervención. El Tottenham había perdido fluidez en sus circulaciones. Pero, a menos de un cuarto de hora para el final, se encontró con un 'regalo' de Mike Penders para ponerse por delante. Tonali botó un saque de esquina, el guardameta belga salió en falso... y Colwill no fue capaz de despejar el balón sobre la línea. Palmer, que ya había sido amonestado por enfrentarse con Mateus Fernandes, cortocircuitó y vio la roja tres minutos después por una dura entrada sobre Gallagher. Ya en superioridad, el Tottenham terminó de resolver el choque a menos de cinco minutos para el final. Tel agarró el balón en campo propio, dejó atrás a Acheampong y batió a Penders con un disparo ajustado al palo corto desde la frontal. La 'Xabineta' se 'cala'... y los 'spurs' empiezan a 'carburar'.

articles.title: Mikautadze destroza al Valencia
articles.standfirst: El georgiano decide el derbi en el añadido y deja a los de Aguirre tiritando
articles.summary: El georgiano decide el derbi en el añadido y deja a los de Aguirre tiritando
articles.body: Estaba el derbi para el empate. Había sido un partido vibrante. Un penalti, un gol anulado, dos rojas, piques, apretones... pero al final el partido lo ganaron los dos mejores jugadores sobre el campo. El partido agonizaba y un balón perdido por el Valencia en área del rival acabó en los pies de Moleiro que puso a correr a Mikautadze y el georgiano no erró en el mano a mano contra Dimitrievski. Los puntos se vana a Villarreal y el Valencia queda destrozado. Muy tocado. Los de Aguirre empezaron ganando, se dejaron empatar y no aprovecharon la superioridad tras la expulsión de Gueye. Elliot se autoexpulsó y en el añadido Moleiro y MIkatadze dieron la puntilla a un Valencia que no reacciona con Aguirre en el banquillo. El fútbol tiene contradicciones maravillosas. Aguirre decidió mandar al banquillo a Raba y jugar con Otorbi en la banda, algo que la grada celebró a lo grande. Era el momento de ver al chaval cabalgar, desbordar, asistir... pero el guión era otro. El grito de Otorbi lesionándose en una de sus explosivas arrancadas silenció Mestalla justo antes de que el mexicano tuviera que dar entrada al sacrificado Raba y la grada le pitara con dureza. Pero como el fútbol hace lo que le da la gana, Raba pasó de los pitos de desprecio a hacer la jugada perfecta que adelantaba al Valencia en el derbi. Una arrancada del extremo y un par de recortes certeros acabaron con Veiga cometiendo penalti sobre el cántabro. Pepelu no falló desde los once metros y a Raba se le puso cara de trabajo bien hecho. "Esto es lo que yo sé hacer", parecía decir so rostro. Antes del gol de los locales, el Villarreal había llevado el peso del partido. Sin alardes, no está para muchas alegrías el equipo de Íñigo, pero dominando. De hecho, la mejor ocasión de la primera parte, penalti al margen, fue de Buchanan. El canadiense se quedó solo ante Dimitrievski tras un desajuste defensivo de los de Aguirre, el mano a mano lo ganó el arquero con una estirada más que meritoria. Con todo el partido se fue al descanso sin mayores contratiempos para ninguno de los dos equipos. Una victoria momentánea de los locales que les daba vida. La segunda mitad arrancó con una gran parada de Gulacsi a Gayá al palo del portero que estuvo a punto de darle otro disgusto a la zaga del Villarreal. El Valencia dominaba y Tárrega encontró el gol tras un par de rechaces tras un córner botado por Javi Guerra que se anuló por fuera de juego. Los locales mostraban las garras queriendo acabar con el partido, pero quedaban muchos kilómetros para llegar a la meta. Los de Aguirre sumaban ocasiones y Danjuma tuvo un mano a mano que tampoco logró embocar. En ese escenario el Villarreal necesitaba reaccionar y poco a poco fue encontrando a un Buchanan que con dos golpeos tremendos estuvo cerca de empatar el partido. Con el partido nivelado, Íñigo sacó a la caballería. Molerio, Cardona y Mikautadze al campo para intentar darle la vuelta a un partido que se les había torcido. Al minuto empataron los amarillos. Desmarque de Cardona y centro preciso para que Freeman, que llegaba en el segundo palo, conectara un cabezazo sin oposición. El gol cambiaba las tornas y el Villarreal parecía despegar con un jugadón de Moleiro que estuvo a punto de adelantar a los amarillos. Pero en ese momento llegó la expulsión de Gueye por propinar un codazo a Gayà. Quedaban diez y el añadido y al Valencia se le aparecía una oportunidad de oro. El Villarreal se recompuso con Comesaña y Pau Navarro para jugar en inferioridad y el Valencia apretó lo que pudo, hasta que Elliott decidió comentar la jugada con el colegiado y llevarse su primera tarjeta roja en España. Con igualdad en el campo los amarillos decidieron aprovechar el regalo y vacunaron a un Valencia que se deshace.

articles.title: José Mourinho responds to Barcelona star’s criticism
articles.summary: Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has on Saturday provided his response to the recent criticism aimed in the direction of he and Los Blancos by Barcelona...
articles.body:
Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has on Saturday provided his response to the recent criticism aimed in the direction of he and Los Blancos by Barcelona star Fermín López.

Real Madrid and Barcelona are of course primed to renew rivalries on Sunday evening, in the season's first edition of El Clásico.

In the buildup to the fixture, much of the media chatter has centred on developments away from the pitch, as those in a position of power at the Santiago Bernabéu continue to seek punishment for their Camp Nou counterparts for their part in the 'Negreira Case'.

Drawn on as much in the days leading up to the fixture, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López admitted:

"Real Madrid's constant references to the Negreira case are getting a bit tiring because we're showing our quality on the pitch. It's unfair to engage in this kind of rhetoric when things are going well for us. If they keep pushing this narrative, it's because it suits them, but we don't get involved in it."

Speaking during his pre-match press conference on Saturday, it therefore came as little surprise when the subject of Fermín's comments was put to the aforementioned José Mourinho.

And Real Madrid's headmaster sniped back, in assuring:

"There are other things that exhaust us, but they keep happening…"

articles.title: Napoli let slip two-goal lead as Roma snatch draw in six-goal thriller
articles.summary: Napoli’s stuttering start in Serie A continued as Roma twice fought back to secure a 3-3 draw in a dramatic Derby del Sole. Frank Anguissa’s brilliant over-h...
articles.body:
Napoli's stuttering start in Serie A continued as Roma twice fought back to secure a 3-3 draw in a dramatic Derby del Sole.

Frank Anguissa's brilliant over-head kick had put the home side in front at the break, with Scott McTominay nodding in a second soon after the restart.

Roma, though, launched a late fightback when Matias Soule reduced the deficit with 20 minutes left and defender Leonardo Balerdi bundled in an equalizer.

Scotland midfielder McTominay – who had scored twice in the 4-3 Champions League win over Bodø/Glimt as his return to action from heart surgery continued – then drilled in a low strike from 20 yards.

Roma, though, hauled themselves back on level terms again in the final minute through a towering header from Balerdi.

Napoli had swept into the lead after 26 minutes through a fine strike from Anguissa.

A free-kick from the left was floated into the Roma area, which was not properly cleared. The ball dropped on the penalty spot for Anguissa, who had his back to goal but spun to dispatch an acrobatic over-head kick looping into the top corner.

McTominay looked to have put the game beyond Roma three minutes into the second half.

The Scotland international met a lofted cross to the back post with a diving header which was scrambled out from behind the line by Roma keeper Pierluigi Gollini, but McTominay then knocked the loose ball back in anyway.

Napoli pulled a goal back with 20 minutes left through Soule's curling left-foot finish before Balerdi bundled in a knockdown from a corner in the 74th minute.

McTominay drilled Napoli back in front for what looked to be a winning goal with seven minutes left, but Roma responded again when Balerdi headed in at the back post.

articles.title: Dortmund beat Frankfurt to go top in Bundesliga
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund returned to winning ways in the Bundesliga with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday to top the table for at leas...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund returned to winning ways in the Bundesliga with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday to top the table for at least one night.

Two substitutes eventually made the difference after Frankfurt had held firm for a long time, as Maximilian Beier curled the winner in the 80th minute off Jobe Bellingham.

Dortmund, who had drawn their two previous league matches, moved three points ahead of champions Bayern Munich who play at third-placed Freiburg on Sunday and will go top again with victory before hosting Dortmund next weekend.

Serhou Guirassy had a dangerous shot in the 15th minute saved by Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Guirassy should have scored two minutes later one on one against the keeper but Atubolu prevailed again with his right arm.

A deflected shot from Daniel Svensson hit the top of the bar, but Frankfurt almost stole a 34th minute lead when a mistake from Felix Nmecha saw Younes Ebnoutalib with only Gregor Kobel to beat but couldn't get the ball past him.

Kobel tipped a shot from Fares Chaibi over the bar shortly after the restart before Guirassy came even closer at the other end when his header off a corner kick hit the crossbar in the 53rd.

Beier came on in the 68th and Bellingham in the 79th. A minute later, the two combined for Beier to curl into the right corner from the edge of the area for a late victory.

In earlier Saturday action, RB Leipzig trounced Elversberg 4-0, Werder Bremen won 3-2 at Mainz, Paderborn defeated SV Hamburg 1-0, Augsburg and Union Berlin drew 1-1 and there were no goals at Cologne v Schalke.

articles.title: El caótico viaje del Oviedo a Almería: ¡aterriza apenas cinco horas antes del partido!
articles.standfirst: La expedición azul aterrizó a las 16:15 horas tras más de cuatro horas de retraso por un problema con el avión previsto
articles.summary: La expedición azul aterrizó a las 16:15 horas tras más de cuatro horas de retraso por un problema con el avión previsto
articles.body: El Real Oviedo aterrizó en Almería apenas cinco horas antes del enfrentamiento de esta noche previsto para las 21:00 horas ante la UD Almería. La expedición asturiana llegó al aeropuerto almeriense a las 16:15 horas, después de una jornada marcada por un importante contratiempo en su desplazamiento, que obligó al equipo a modificar por completo su hoja de ruta antes de poner rumbo al sur. A su llegada, el autobús del club esperaba desde hacía horas en la terminal para trasladar directamente a jugadores y cuerpo técnico al hotel de concentración. Allí fueron recibidos por un pequeño grupo de aficionados oviedistas que quiso mostrar su apoyo antes de un duelo de máxima exigencia frente al líder de LaLiga Hypermotion. Todo comenzó a complicarse a primera hora de la mañana. El vuelo chárter del conjunto carbayón debía despegar desde el Aeropuerto de Asturias a las 10:30 horas, pero el avión encargado de realizar el trayecto nunca llegó a aterrizar por un problema completamente ajeno tanto a las condiciones meteorológicas como a la operativa del propio aeropuerto. La plantilla tuvo que permanecer durante varias horas en las instalaciones aeroportuarias a la espera de una solución. Finalmente, la expedición pudo reanudar sus planes gracias a una aeronave enviada desde Valencia, que tomó tierra en Asturias poco después de las 14:15 horas. Tras un embarque acelerado, el Oviedo despegó rumbo a Almería en un vuelo de alrededor de hora y cuarto que transcurrió sin incidencias, poniendo fin a una mañana de incertidumbre antes de centrarse definitivamente en el importante encuentro de esta noche.

articles.title: Eddie Howe can repeat his genius Joelinton masterstroke with this Man United star waiting to be unleashed
articles.summary: Fabian Hürzeler has dismissed speculation that he is set to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.At the same time, Antonio Conte has insisted that cl...
articles.body:
Fabian Hürzeler has dismissed speculation that he is set to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

At the same time, Antonio Conte has insisted that claims of him being in talks with a top club are unfounded and that he is not pushing for an immediate return to management.

United, for their part, are not keen on Conte, with reports suggesting Ineos do not view him as the right fit for their project.

Should Carrick be dismissed, however, the contest now feels like a two-horse race between Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann .

While Nagelsmann's tactical sharpness could make him an upgrade on Carrick, if I were calling the shots, I would still opt for Howe.

Howe is Premier League proven. At Bournemouth, he kept the club in the top flight for five consecutive seasons, a remarkable achievement that earned him Football League Manager of the Decade .

At Newcastle, he restored the club's competitive edge and gave them a clear identity. He eventually guided them back into the Champions League for the first time in 20 years.

At both clubs, he established himself as one of the most successful managers of their modern eras.

The main argument against Howe is that, while he might fix what is broken at United, just as he did at Newcastle, he may lack the final ingredient needed to push the team over the line and deliver a 21st league title.

Critics are quick to point out that he never transformed Newcastle into genuine title challengers.

Yet that argument is illogical. Despite having some of the richest owners in world football, Newcastle often struggled in the transfer market.

Howe wanted the very front three United now possess, Matheus Cunha , Benjamin Šeško and Bryan Mbeumo , but all three rejected the chance to join him. As a result, the Toons endured one of their most disappointing summer windows in 2025.

Had Howe secured those players and avoided the injury problems that followed, Newcastle's 2025-26 campaign could have looked very different.

If Jason Wilcox goes ahead and hires Howe, fans will naturally look to him to get the best out of Cunha, Mbeumo and Šeško. Still, one player I believe could be massively revitalised is Joshua Zirkzee .

Zirkzee could be Eddie Howe's Joelinton at Man United

When Newcastle signed Joelinton from Hoffenheim in 2019, they were convinced they had secured a centre-forward who would light up the Premier League. Instead, the Brazilian struggled to find the net.

There were calls for the Magpies to cut their losses and sign a proven goalscorer. Howe, however, saw something in the Samba star. He recognised Joelinton's physicality and combativeness, and saw them as perfect for a box-to-box midfield role. It proved a masterstroke.

With Joelinton anchoring the engine room, Howe built one of the league's most formidable midfields, a unit opposition sides genuinely feared.

Zirkzee may not possess the same combative edge as Joelinton, yet he shares a similar capacity for reinvention.

Deployed in a number 10 role, the Dutchman could flourish. His game is built more around creativity and connection than pure centre-forward play.

He excels at receiving the ball under pressure, escaping markers and driving the team forward from deeper positions into the final third.

Beyond that, his sharp one-twos and ability to link play could give United a valuable alternative creative outlet on days when Bruno Fernandes is not at his sharpest, as in recent matches.

Carrick experimented with Zirkzee in the number 10 role during pre-season, and he was class. However, the United coach has been reluctant to trust him there in competitive fixtures so far. Howe is unlikely to share that caution.

In the end, giving Zirkzee a chance to reinvent himself as a playmaker should not only unlock his best qualities but also help the 20-time English champions to hold on to a baller who remains popular in the dressing room and so contributes positively to squad harmony.

articles.title: Spalletti could be two games away from the sack at Juventus
articles.summary: Juventus cannot afford to spend another season without Champions League football, and the club could be ready to dismiss Luciano Spalletti if results fail to...
articles.body:
Juventus cannot afford to spend another season without Champions League football, and the club could be ready to dismiss Luciano Spalletti if results fail to improve. The Bianconeri are determined to secure a place among Serie A's top four, and continued inconsistency could force the hierarchy to consider a change in the dugout.

Spalletti has now spent around a year on the Juventus bench, and this is his first full season in charge of the club. Expectations remain high, with the manager expected to deliver consistent victories and guide the team towards its objectives. However, Juventus have struggled to maintain the required level of performance, leaving his position under increasing pressure.

The club needs a strong response from its players, but the responsibility also rests with Spalletti to find solutions and restore confidence. With Champions League qualification such an important target, Juventus may have little patience if their results continue to disappoint.

Juventus consider their managerial options

The Bianconeri have been linked with potential moves for Antonio Conte and Simone Inzaghi in recent weeks. Both managers have considerable experience at the highest level, and their names have emerged as possible alternatives should Juventus decide to make a change.

The Old Lady has shown that it is willing to dismiss managers when performances fall below expectations. That history means Spalletti cannot assume his position is secure, particularly with the club facing an important period in its campaign.

According to a report involving Giuseppe Falci, Juventus could decide to sack Spalletti if the results of their next two matches fail to meet expectations. The upcoming fixtures could therefore prove decisive for the manager as he attempts to keep the club on course for its objectives.

Two matches could decide Spalletti's future

Juventus face Lecce and Genoa in their next two games, both away from home. These are fixtures the club will expect to win if it is serious about securing a place in the Serie A top four by the end of the season.

Failure to collect the required points in either match would increase the pressure, while disappointing results in both could leave the club considering an immediate managerial change. Spalletti will therefore understand the importance of producing positive performances and results.

Falci discussed the situation via Tuttojuve , stating:

"Spalletti's future hangs on the next two matches, both away: Lecce and Genoa."

articles.title: Texas QB Arch Manning Faces Major Development Before Ole Miss Game
articles.summary: The No. 19 Texas Longhorns have their backs against the wall entering Saturday night’s showdown against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels. Texas has lost back-to-bac...
articles.body:
The No. 19 Texas Longhorns have their backs against the wall entering Saturday night's showdown against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels.

Texas has lost back-to-back games over the last two weeks, falling to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators, both of whom were unranked at the time of the losses.

Now, Texas returns home to Austin under immense pressure, particularly on head coach Steve Sarkisian and quarterback Arch Manning to deliver against an Ole Miss team that has proven it can hang with just about anybody in the SEC.

Ahead of the matchup, ESPN's Pete Thamel appeared on "College GameDay" and doubled down on his report earlier this week, revealing that Manning took "significantly fewer" first-team reps in practice this week while backup KJ Lacey Jr. saw an uptick."I'm gonna die on the hill of letting it rip," Manning said.

"Arch Manning took significantly less first-team reps with Texas' first-team offense this week than he usually does," Thamel said. "Let's be clear, Steve Sarkisian does not want to replace Arch Manning as his starter. But he has started to prepare to do that if Arch Manning struggles. Backup KJ Lacey Jr. had a precipitous uptick in first-team reps."

This raises the question of whether Sarkisian would turn to Lacey Jr. if Manning struggles in the first half against Ole Miss. With Texas fighting to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, another loss would make its path to the postseason significantly more difficult.

This week, Sarkisian revealed that Manning has adopted an "edgy" mindset as he looks to bounce back and silence his critics.

"I would use the word edgy, and I like it," Sarkisian told reporters Thursday, via Inside Texas. "He's edgy right now. And I think that somebody texted me today that we lost the 'Aw Shucks' kid, and we created something else. I don't know if we lost him, we created this, we did, all of us. Y'all included me, the whole thing, right? Everybody on ESPN, we've created this. And so we'll see what comes out of it. But he's edgy right now. And honestly, I appreciate that about him. At some point, he's gotta fight back. And the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates, and enjoy playing football with his teammates. And so I'm looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night."

articles.title: Jobe Bellingham 'reconecta' a un Dortmund que se acuesta líder
articles.standfirst: El hermano menor de Jude entró desde el banquillo y asistió a Beier para consumar el triunfo ante el Eintracht
articles.summary: El hermano menor de Jude entró desde el banquillo y asistió a Beier para consumar el triunfo ante el Eintracht
articles.body: Los empates ante Werder Bremen y Unión Berlín habían frenado el impecable inicio de un Borussia Dortmund que se fue al parón con pleno de victorias en Bundesliga. El Signal Iduna Park ya se olía el tercero consecutivo frente al Eintracht (1-0). Jode Bellingham, sin embargo, entró desde el banquillo para asistir a Beier y lograr un triunfo que les permite dormir líderes. Se reencontraba Niko Kovac con un Eintracht Frankfurt al que guio a la conquista de la POKAL en 2018 antes de poner rumbo al Bayern Múnich. Sin Karetsas, lesionado, no tiró de Nwaneri... sino que reforzó el centro del campo con Veerman, Nmecha y Sabitzer. Arriba, Guirassy y Fábio Silva formaron dupla. Pocas veces desde la llegada de Kovac se ha visto a un Dortmund tan fluido como en el arranque de partido. La movilidad y la rapidez en sus ataques asfixiaron a un Eintracht que logro sostenerse gracias a las intervenciones de Atubolu. Pasado el primer cuarto de hora, el ex del Friburgo le sacó dos manos meritorias a Guirassy. No despertó el Eintracht hasta que, en el 26', Burkardt cruzó en exceso un remate desde la frontal que no puso en apuros a un Gregor Kobel que sí tuvo que achicar en el 33' ante Ebnoutalib. Entre medias, Svensson, previo desvío de un defensor, mandó una volea al larguero. El caudal ofensivo del Dortmund, eso sí, se había rebajado bastante antes del descanso. Chaibi, en la primera jugada de la primera parte, trató de sorprender a Kobel aprovechando el humo provocado por las bengalas encendidas detrás de su portería. Guirassy, por su parte, seguía a lo suyo: envío un remate al larguero a centro de Veerman y, poco después, mandó otro fuera. Kovac intervino con poco más de 20' por delante dando entrada a Beier, Chukwuemeka y un Nwaneri que probó disparo en el primer balón que recibió. Poco después, el propio Chukwuemeka reclamó un penalti después de que su disparo topase con la mano de Brassier. Los cambios elevaron el ritmo y, nada más saltar al césped, Jobe Bellingham asistió a Beier: rompió en profundidad, maniobró sobre la línea de fondo y cedió atrás para que el alemán ajustase al palo largo desde el 'piquito' del área.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund player ratings vs Eintracht Frankfurt: Beier and Bellingham's instant impact off the bench keeps Kovač's men top of the Bundesliga
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund stayed top of the Bundesliga with a hard-fought, tactically disciplined 1-0 win over a resilient Eintracht Frankfurt side at Signal Iduna P...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund stayed top of the Bundesliga with a hard-fought, tactically disciplined 1-0 win over a resilient Eintracht Frankfurt side at Signal Iduna Park.

Niko Kovač's men dominated the territorial battle, enjoying 58.4% possession and firing 18 shots, but struggled to break down a compact Frankfurt block that racked up 48 clearances. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 80th minute, and Kovač's bold changes were behind it. Substitutes Maximilian Beier and Jobe Bellingham added verticality and edge, combining brilliantly to unlock the stalemate and secure three vital points in the title race.

Gregor Kobel - 8/10 A solid, reliable display from the Swiss international. He stayed alert to make three important saves, most notably denying Farès Chaïbi early in the second half, and his distribution was key to Dortmund building from the back.

Ramy Bensebaini - 8/10 Occupying the left side of Kovač's back three, the Algerian was immense. He was dominant in the air, strong in the tackle and helped keep Frankfurt's attack largely quiet.

Nico Schlotterbeck - 7/10 The captain marshalled the defensive line with authority. His ability to step into midfield and break lines mattered in a game where Frankfurt sat deep, and he anchored a backline that limited the visitors to three shots on target.

Waldemar Anton - 7.5/10 Anton provided the necessary cover on the right of the back three. Disciplined in his positioning, he denied Frankfurt space in behind and played a big part in the clean sheet.

Julian Ryerson - 7/10 Operating as the right wing-back in the 3-4-2-1, Ryerson offered his usual industry. He created two chances and had a late one of his own, firing just high, before being replaced by Joane Gadou in stoppage time.

Joey Veerman - 8.5/10 The heartbeat of the team and arguably the man of the match. The Dutchman set the tempo in the centre of the pitch, constantly scanning and orchestrating Dortmund's passing moves. His pinpoint deliveries created several high-quality chances, including Guirassy's header that hit the crossbar.

Felix Nmecha - 7/10 A busy display in the double pivot before he made way for Jobe Bellingham. Nmecha did more than keep the ball moving; he kept arriving around the box, seeing one effort saved and two more blocked as he tried to force the issue.

Daniel Svensson - 7/10 Operating as the left wing-back, Svensson struggled to consistently get past Frankfurt's tight marking. He delivered a good early cross for Fábio Silva but was sacrificed in the 68th minute as Kovač went for a more attacking approach.

Marcel Sabitzer - 6/10 Starting as one of the two attacking midfielders, Sabitzer worked hard between the lines, but space was at a premium against Koch and Brassier. He was part of the triple substitution in the 68th minute.

Fábio Silva - 7/10 The Portuguese forward showed flashes of his technical quality, heading just over early on and setting up Guirassy for a first-half effort. He was largely crowded out before being replaced by Ethan Nwaneri.

Serhou Guirassy - 7/10 The focal point of the attack and a constant physical handful for Frankfurt's defence. He tested Noah Atubolu twice in the first half and was unlucky not to score when his 53rd-minute header crashed off the crossbar.

Maximilian Beier - 8.5/10 The hero of the night. Introduced in the 68th minute, Beier changed the dynamic of the attack at once. His right-footed strike from outside the box in the 80th minute was a moment of pure quality, finding the top corner to break the deadlock.

Jobe Bellingham - 8/10 Bellingham made a huge impact despite coming on only in the 79th minute. A minute later, he provided the assist for Beier's winner, and he added smart defensive work in the closing stages to help see out the win.

Carney Chukwuemeka - 7/10 Brought on for Sabitzer to add physicality and drive, Chukwuemeka did exactly that and more. He was a creative spark, setting up chances for Nwaneri, Nmecha and Ryerson shortly after his introduction.

Ethan Nwaneri - 6.5/10 The teenager showed impressive composure after replacing Fábio Silva. He forced a sharp save from Atubolu almost immediately and kept the ball moving quickly in the final third.

Joane Gadou - N/A A stoppage-time (90+2) substitution to run down the clock and shore up the defence.

Niko Kovač - 8.5/10 Kovač deserves full credit for this victory. Recognising that his starting attackers were being stifled, he changed the game with his 68th-minute triple substitution. Bringing on Beier, Chukwuemeka and later Bellingham proved a masterstroke.

articles.title: Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. Suspended by Alabama for Violation of Team Rules
articles.summary: Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. has been suspended for violating team rules, a team spokesperson told On3's Charlie Potter.
articles.body:
Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. has been suspended for violating team rules, a team spokesperson told On3's Charlie Potter .

Kirkpatrick was ruled out on Alabama's final SEC availability report released 90 minutes before Saturday's 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff against visiting Texas A&M.

He had appeared in every game of Alabama's 5-2 start to the 2026 season.

Alabama previously suspended Kirkpatrick in November 2025, after which he sat out the final seven games of last season.

articles.title: Burnley: Nicky Hayen sacked after thrashing at Lincoln with Clarets in Championship relegation zone
articles.summary: Nicky Hayen was appointed Burnley boss in July but has been sacked just 12 games into the Championship table with one of the pre-season promotion favourites in the relegation zone; Hayen won just one game in the league and his side lost 4-1 at Lincoln on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Belgian took charge in the summer but has overseen just one win from their club's first 12 Championship fixtures and the Clarets were beaten 4-1 at Lincoln on Saturday.

Hayen apologised to the Burnley supporters for the performance after the game.

In pre-season, Burnley had been among the favourites for promotion and to make an immediate return to the Premier League but are third-bottom and in the Championship relegation zone. They have the joint-worst defensive record in the league.

A 26-word statement from Burnley announcing his sacking read:

"Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."

Hayen's reign began with a Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over League One Notts County but they were knocked out in the next round on spot kicks by Bradford.

Hayen's only other win came in a 4-0 victory at Watford on October 10.

Speaking to the media following the loss to Lincoln, Hayen said: "It's the same story of the season for us that we keep conceding easy goals and you saw that in the second half.

"They want to work hard, but you have to show it. What we do in training is really good, but we can't execute that the same way in the games. Is that pressure? I don't know.

"It's frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn't matter because it's another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

"We haven't got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops.

"I don't know (if I will still be in charge). I know it's a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board."

articles.title: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham: Mike Penders error and Mathys Tel earn Spurs rare victory at Stamford Bridge as Cole Palmer sent off
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Tottenham earn rare victory at Chelsea; Mike Penders punched ball into his own net before Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card after escaping a straight red earlier; Mathys Tel secured statement win under Roberto De Zerbi with brilliant solo goal
articles.body:
Spurs had won only one of their previous 36 league visits to Chelsea, but delivered their best performance yet under Roberto De Zerbi, earning back-to-back wins within six days and easing concerns about a third season in the bottom half of the Premier League.

Xabi Alonso decided to play without a recognised striker in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro, handing a first start to 19-year-old winger Geovany Quenda and playing Morgan Rogers through the middle instead of leading the line with the experienced Danny Welbeck.

Tottenham had 70 per cent possession in the first half and should have led when Omar Marmoush wasted a big chance from close-range. Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made saves from Cole Palmer, Jordan Henderson and Morgan Rogers, but it was clear Alonso needed to change his line-up at half-time.

Instead, he stuck with it, and Tottenham became more dominant, despite losing James Maddison to injury early in the second half, and eventually took the lead when Penders punched Mateus Fernandes' corner into his own net under pressure from Spurs centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke.

Chelsea's evening quickly worsened when Palmer received a second yellow card for standing on Conor Gallagher in a tackle

Palmer had "lost his head", according to Sky Sports' Gary Neville, after earlier escaping a red card for barging into Fernandes' head when the Spurs midfielder was kneeling on the ground after stopping the Chelsea forward with a handball.

Tottenham could not lose from there with 10 minutes left, but Tel made sure with a brilliant solo goal. He drove in from deep on the left, cut inside, and fired low into the bottom-left corner to cap a statement victory under De Zerbi.

The stats behind Chelsea's horror show vs Spurs

Spurs have beaten Chelsea in all competitions at Stamford Bridge while keeping a clean sheet for the first time since December 1986 (also 2-0).

Chelsea failed to score at home in a Premier League London derby for just the second time in their last 17 such games, after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace last season.

Chelsea have conceded eight set-piece goals in the Premier League this season, double any other side.

Mike Penders became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in a Premier League match, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.

Chelsea had just seven attempts against Spurs, their fewest in a Premier League game this season and their fewest at home in the competition since January against Brentford (6).
